Q90.name: Paris
facts: Home to the Eiffel Tower, built for the 1889 World's Fair.
The Seine flows through the city, past Notre-Dame cathedral on the Île de la Cité.
The Louvre here holds the Mona Lisa and is the world's most-visited art museum.

Q84.name: London
facts: The River Thames runs through it, past the Tower and the Houses of Parliament with Big Ben.
It opened the world's first underground railway, in 1863.
The only city to have hosted the Summer Olympics three times: 1908, 1948 and 2012.

Q220.name: Rome
facts: Home to the Colosseum, the Pantheon and the Trevi Fountain.
Legend says it was founded by the twins Romulus and Remus, raised by a she-wolf.
Built on seven hills beside the River Tiber; spaghetti carbonara is its signature pasta.

Q237.name: Vatican City
facts: The world's smallest sovereign state, ruled by the pope.
Michelangelo painted the ceiling of its Sistine Chapel, where popes are elected.
Guarded by the Swiss Guard, in uniforms with blue, red and yellow stripes.

Q64.name: Berlin
facts: A wall divided the city into East and West from 1961 until 1989.
The Brandenburg Gate and the glass-domed Reichstag stand here, near the River Spree.
Currywurst, sausage with curry ketchup, is its famous street snack.

Q649.name: Moscow
facts: Home to the Kremlin, Red Square and the onion-domed St. Basil's Cathedral.
Napoleon captured it in 1812, only to see it burn and retreat in winter.
Its metro stations are famous for chandeliers, mosaics and marble halls.

Q1218.name: Jerusalem
facts: Its walled Old City holds the Western Wall, the Dome of the Rock and the Church of the Holy Sepulchre.
Holy to Jews, Christians and Muslims alike.
The Mount of Olives overlooks the city; the Dead Sea lies a short drive east.

Q1741.name: Vienna
facts: Mozart, Beethoven and Schubert all worked here; it's the home of the waltz.
Sigmund Freud developed psychoanalysis here; his Berggasse 19 practice is now a museum.
The Danube flows past it; Sachertorte chocolate cake was created here.

Q334.name: Singapore
facts: A tiny island city-state at the southern tip of the Malay Peninsula.
Famous for its Merlion statue, Marina Bay Sands and the Supertrees of Gardens by the Bay.
Selling chewing gum has been banned here since 1992.

Q270.name: Warsaw
facts: Its Old Town was rebuilt almost from scratch after near-total destruction in World War II.
Marie Curie was born here; Chopin grew up here.
It lies on the Vistula River, and its symbol is a sword-wielding mermaid.

Q1085.name: Prague
facts: Its medieval Astronomical Clock, from 1410, still performs every hour.
The statue-lined Charles Bridge crosses the Vltava River here.
Franz Kafka was born here; its castle is one of the largest ancient castle complexes.

Q656.name: Saint Petersburg
facts: Founded by Peter the Great in 1703 on the Neva River delta at the Baltic Sea.
Home to the Hermitage museum in the former Winter Palace of the tsars.
Known as Leningrad, it survived a nearly 900-day siege in World War II.

Q1489.name: Mexico City
facts: Built on the ruins of Tenochtitlan, the Aztec capital that stood on an island in a lake.
Its Estadio Azteca hosted two World Cup finals, in 1970 and 1986.
Frida Kahlo's Blue House is in its Coyoacán district; the city sits about 2,240 m high.

Q1486.name: Buenos Aires
facts: The birthplace of the tango.
Lies on the Río de la Plata; its Avenida 9 de Julio is one of the widest avenues in the world.
Pope Francis was born here; Eva Perón is buried in its Recoleta Cemetery.

Q235.name: Monaco
facts: The world's second-smallest country, on the Riviera near Nice.
Hosts a Formula One Grand Prix on its twisting streets, and the Monte Carlo Casino.
Hollywood star Grace Kelly married its Prince Rainier III in 1956.

Q1757.name: Helsinki
facts: The Suomenlinna sea fortress, on islands off its harbour, is a UNESCO site.
Linus Torvalds was born here and began creating Linux as a student at its university.
A short ferry ride across the Baltic links it with Tallinn; it hosted the 1952 Olympics.

Q1490.name: Tokyo
facts: Formerly called Edo, it was the seat of the shoguns.
Home to the Shibuya scramble crossing and the Skytree, with Mount Fuji visible on clear days.
Hosted the Summer Olympics in 1964 and again in 2021.

Q61.name: Washington, D.C.
facts: Home to the White House, the Capitol and the Lincoln Memorial.
Sits on the Potomac River; it was planned by Pierre L'Enfant in the 1790s.
Its famous cherry trees were a gift from the mayor of Tokyo in 1912.

Q60.name: New York City
facts: The Statue of Liberty greets ships in its harbour at the mouth of the Hudson River.
Home to Central Park, Times Square, Broadway and Wall Street.
Nicknamed the Big Apple; its Empire State Building was the world's tallest from 1931 to 1970.

Q1781.name: Budapest
facts: The Danube divides it into hilly Buda on the west and flat Pest on the east.
Ernő Rubik invented his famous cube here in 1974.
Famous for thermal baths like Széchenyi and a grand neo-Gothic Parliament on the river.

Q956.name: Beijing
facts: Home to the Forbidden City, Tiananmen Square and the Temple of Heaven.
The first city to host both the Summer (2008) and Winter (2022) Olympics.
Famous for Peking duck; sections of the Great Wall lie just north of it.

Q1899.name: Kyiv
facts: Stands on the Dnieper River; its St. Sophia Cathedral dates from the 11th century.
Its Maidan square was the centre of the 2004 Orange Revolution and 2013-14 protests.
The cave monastery of Pechersk Lavra is here; Chernobyl lies about 100 km north.

Q8684.name: Seoul
facts: Sits on the Han River; the demilitarized zone lies only about 50 km to the north.
Hosted the 1988 Summer Olympics; Psy's Gangnam Style is named after one of its districts.
The Joseon-era Gyeongbokgung Palace and Namsan Tower are among its landmarks.

Q597.name: Lisbon
facts: A huge earthquake and tsunami destroyed much of it in 1755.
Custard tarts (pastéis de nata) come from the monks of its Jerónimos Monastery in Belém.
Built on hills by the Tagus estuary; its red suspension bridge resembles the Golden Gate.

Q3616.name: Tehran
facts: Sits at the foot of the Alborz mountains, with snowy Mount Damavand visible nearby.
Churchill, Roosevelt and Stalin met here in 1943.
Landmarks include the white Azadi Tower and the tall Milad Tower.

Q8678.name: Rio de Janeiro
facts: The Christ the Redeemer statue overlooks it from Corcovado mountain.
Famous for Copacabana and Ipanema beaches and its Sugarloaf Mountain cable car.
Hosts the world's most famous Carnival, and the 2016 Summer Olympics.

Q727.name: Amsterdam
facts: Famous for its 17th-century canal ring, and more bicycles than residents.
Anne Frank hid from the Nazis in a house here, now a museum.
The Rijksmuseum here displays Rembrandt's The Night Watch.

Q406.name: Istanbul
facts: Straddles the Bosphorus, with parts on both the European and Asian sides.
Formerly Byzantium and then Constantinople, capital of the Byzantine and Ottoman empires.
Home to Hagia Sophia, the Blue Mosque and the Grand Bazaar.

Q1524.name: Athens
facts: The Parthenon stands on its Acropolis, a temple to its patron goddess.
Considered the birthplace of democracy; Socrates and Plato taught here.
Hosted the first modern Olympic Games in 1896.

Q1754.name: Stockholm
facts: Built on 14 islands where Lake Mälaren meets the Baltic Sea.
The Nobel Prizes (except Peace) are awarded here every December.
The Vasa museum shows a warship that sank on its maiden voyage in 1628; there's an ABBA museum too.

Q1861.name: Bangkok
facts: Its full ceremonial name is the world's longest place name; locals call it Krung Thep.
The Grand Palace, Wat Arun and the Emerald Buddha line the Chao Phraya River.
Backpacker hub Khao San Road and tuk-tuks are famous here.

Q3630.name: Jakarta
facts: Known as Batavia under Dutch rule, on the northwest coast of Java.
Parts of the city are sinking so fast that the capital is being moved to Borneo.
Its National Monument (Monas) is an obelisk topped with a gold-leaf flame.

Q8646.name: Hong Kong
facts: A British colony until 1997, now run under one country, two systems.
Victoria Harbour, the Star Ferry and the view from the Peak are famous sights.
Bruce Lee grew up here; it's renowned for dim sum and its dense skyscraper skyline.

Q2841.name: Bogotá
facts: Sits on a high Andean plateau about 2,640 m above sea level.
Its Gold Museum holds a huge collection of pre-Hispanic gold, including the El Dorado raft.
Every Sunday its Ciclovía closes over 100 km of roads to cars for cyclists.

Q1492.name: Barcelona
facts: Gaudí's still-unfinished Sagrada Família basilica is here, begun in 1882.
Hosted the 1992 Summer Olympics; its football club plays at the Camp Nou.
La Rambla boulevard runs down to the Mediterranean; Park Güell is another Gaudí gem.

Q1748.name: Copenhagen
facts: The Little Mermaid statue honours Hans Christian Andersen, who lived here.
Tivoli Gardens, opened in 1843, is one of the world's oldest amusement parks.
The Øresund Bridge links it to Malmö in Sweden; colourful Nyhavn harbour is iconic.

Q1761.name: Dublin
facts: The River Liffey runs through it; Guinness has been brewed at St. James's Gate since 1759.
James Joyce's Ulysses is set here on 16 June 1904, celebrated as Bloomsday.
Trinity College here displays the Book of Kells; the 1916 Easter Rising began here.

Q472.name: Sofia
facts: The gold-domed Alexander Nevsky Cathedral is its most famous landmark.
Sits at the foot of Mount Vitosha, a popular ski and hiking area.
Its motto is grows but does not age; mineral springs flow in the city centre.

Q65.name: Los Angeles
facts: Home to Hollywood, the Hollywood sign and the Walk of Fame.
The Academy Awards (Oscars) are held here every year.
Hosted the Olympics in 1932 and 1984, and will again in 2028.

Q1530.name: Baghdad
facts: Founded in 762 as a round city on the Tigris River by the Abbasid caliph al-Mansur.
Its House of Wisdom was a great centre of learning in the Islamic Golden Age.
Many One Thousand and One Nights tales are set here, in the time of Harun al-Rashid.

Q1297.name: Chicago
facts: Sits on Lake Michigan; the river through downtown is dyed green every St. Patrick's Day.
A Great Fire destroyed much of it in 1871; it then built the world's first skyscraper.
Famous for deep-dish pizza, the Willis (Sears) Tower and the Cloud Gate Bean sculpture.

Q2887.name: Santiago
facts: Sits in a valley with the snow-capped Andes as its backdrop.
Founded by conquistador Pedro de Valdivia in 1541, on the Mapocho River.
Cerro San Cristóbal hill, topped by a statue of the Virgin Mary, overlooks the city.

Q585.name: Oslo
facts: The Nobel Peace Prize is awarded here every December.
Edvard Munch's The Scream hangs in its museums; Vigeland Park holds 200+ sculptures.
Lies at the head of a long fjord; the Holmenkollen ski jump towers above it.

Q34600.name: Kyoto
facts: The imperial capital for over a thousand years, until 1869.
Famous for the Golden Pavilion, Fushimi Inari's thousands of torii gates, and geisha in Gion.
Its temples were spared from bombing in World War II for their cultural value.

Q2844.name: Brasília
facts: A planned capital built in the 1950s and inaugurated in 1960.
Lúcio Costa's plan is shaped like an airplane or bird; Oscar Niemeyer designed its buildings.
Sits on a high central plateau beside an artificial lake, Lake Paranoá.

Q1930.name: Ottawa
facts: Queen Victoria chose it as the capital in 1857, partly as a compromise.
In winter its Rideau Canal becomes one of the world's largest skating rinks.
Its tulip festival honours bulbs gifted by the Dutch royal family after World War II.

Q9248.name: Baku
facts: Lies on the Caspian Sea, on the Absheron Peninsula.
Its Flame Towers skyline glows like fire; the region was an early oil boomtown.
Known as the City of Winds; it hosted Eurovision in 2012 and an F1 street race.

Q14773.name: Macau
facts: A Portuguese colony until 1999, the last European colony in Asia.
Its gambling industry is the world's biggest, outearning Las Vegas.
Famous for the Ruins of St. Paul's facade and Portuguese-style egg tarts.

Q490.name: Milan
facts: Leonardo da Vinci's Last Supper is painted on a refectory wall here.
Home to the Gothic Duomo cathedral and the La Scala opera house.
A fashion capital; its rival clubs AC and Inter share the San Siro stadium.

Q1773.name: Riga
facts: Has one of the world's greatest concentrations of Art Nouveau buildings.
Lies on the Daugava River near the Baltic Sea.
Black Balsam, a dark herbal liqueur, is its traditional drink.

Q2868.name: Lima
facts: Founded by Francisco Pizarro in 1535 as the City of Kings.
Sits on the Pacific coast desert; it hardly ever rains, but a grey fog (garúa) is common.
Famous for ceviche and as a world capital of gastronomy.

Q3711.name: Belgrade
facts: Stands where the Sava River flows into the Danube.
Its Kalemegdan fortress overlooks the rivers; it has been destroyed dozens of times.
Tennis star Novak Djokovic was born here; it has a Nikola Tesla Museum.

Q1410.name: Gibraltar
facts: Dominated by the Rock, a limestone peak at the entrance to the Mediterranean.
Home to Europe's only wild monkeys, the Barbary macaques.
Its main road crosses the airport runway, so traffic stops for planes.

Q3130.name: Sydney
facts: Its Opera House, with sail-like roofs, sits beside the Harbour Bridge.
Famous for Bondi Beach and spectacular New Year's Eve fireworks over the harbour.
Hosted the 2000 Summer Olympics.

Q987.name: New Delhi
facts: Designed by architects Edwin Lutyens and Herbert Baker in the 1910s-20s.
The presidential palace Rashtrapati Bhavan sits at the end of a grand ceremonial avenue.
The lotus-shaped Bahá'í House of Worship is a famous landmark here.

Q3640.name: Ankara
facts: Became the capital in 1923, chosen by Mustafa Kemal Atatürk.
Atatürk's mausoleum, Anıtkabir, stands on a hill here.
Angora cats, goats and rabbits are named after its old name, Angora.

Q8686.name: Shanghai
facts: Its riverfront Bund faces the futuristic skyline of Pudong across the Huangpu River.
Lies near the mouth of the Yangtze, the world's busiest container port.
Its maglev train to the airport hits 300 km/h; soup dumplings (xiaolongbao) are its signature.

Q5465.name: Cape Town
facts: Flat-topped Table Mountain rises behind the city.
Nelson Mandela was imprisoned for 18 years on Robben Island, off its coast.
The Cape of Good Hope lies nearby; penguins live on Boulders Beach.

Q3870.name: Nairobi
facts: Its national park has lions and giraffes with skyscrapers in the background.
Its name comes from a Maasai phrase meaning cool water.
Karen Blixen, author of Out of Africa, lived on a farm on its outskirts.

Q1858.name: Hanoi
facts: Hoan Kiem Lake, with a turtle legend, lies in the heart of the city.
Ho Chi Minh's embalmed body lies in a mausoleum here.
Lies on the Red River; its Old Quarter is known for 36 guild streets and pho.

Q239.name: Brussels
facts: Home to the European Union's main institutions and NATO headquarters.
Famous for the Manneken Pis statue, the Atomium and the Grand-Place square.
Known for waffles, chocolate and comics; Tintin creator Hergé was born here.

Q11194.name: Sarajevo
facts: Archduke Franz Ferdinand's assassination here in 1914 sparked World War I.
Hosted the 1984 Winter Olympics.
Endured a siege from 1992 to 1996, the longest of a capital in modern warfare.

Q994.name: Tbilisi
facts: Its name comes from the word for warm, after its sulphur hot springs.
Sits on the Kura (Mtkvari) River below the hilltop Narikala fortress.
Famous for khachapuri cheese bread and ancient winemaking in clay vessels.

Q1354.name: Dhaka
facts: Known as the rickshaw capital of the world.
Lies on the Buriganga River in the Ganges delta.
Famous for muslin cloth in history and for its Parliament building by Louis Kahn.

Q1854.name: Ho Chi Minh City
facts: Formerly called Saigon; its fall to northern forces in 1975 ended a long war.
Lies on the Saigon River near the vast Mekong Delta.
Famous for its motorbike-filled streets, Ben Thanh Market and a French-built cathedral.

Q19689.name: Tirana
facts: Its central Skanderbeg Square honours a 15th-century national hero.
Former bunkers from the communist era have been turned into Bunk'Art museums.
Its once-grey buildings were painted in bright colours in the 2000s.

Q1865.name: Kuala Lumpur
facts: The Petronas Twin Towers were the world's tallest buildings from 1998 to 2004.
Its name means muddy confluence, where the Klang and Gombak rivers meet.
The Batu Caves Hindu shrine, with a giant golden statue, is on its edge.

Q62.name: San Francisco
facts: The Golden Gate Bridge spans the strait at the entrance to its bay.
Famous for cable cars, steep hills and the island prison of Alcatraz.
Largely destroyed by an earthquake and fire in 1906; Levi Strauss founded his jeans company here.

Q3114.name: Canberra
facts: A purpose-built capital, chosen as a compromise between Sydney and Melbourne.
Designed by Chicago architects Walter Burley Griffin and Marion Mahony Griffin.
Built around an artificial lake named after its designer.

Q1770.name: Tallinn
facts: Its medieval walled Old Town is one of the best preserved in Europe.
Lies on the Baltic coast, a short ferry ride across the water from Helsinki.
Skype's software was developed here, and it holds a huge choir song festival.

Q1780.name: Bratislava
facts: The only capital bordering two other countries: Austria and Hungary.
Lies on the Danube, with a boxy castle on a hill above the river.
Hungarian kings were crowned in its St. Martin's Cathedral for centuries.

Q174.name: São Paulo
facts: The largest city in the Southern Hemisphere.
Has the world's largest Japanese community outside Japan, in its Liberdade district.
F1 legend Ayrton Senna was born here; it hosts a Grand Prix at Interlagos.

Q3141.name: Melbourne
facts: Hosts a Grand Slam tennis tournament every January.
Famous for trams, laneway coffee culture and a 100,000-seat cricket ground.
Lies on the Yarra River at Port Phillip Bay; hosted the 1956 Olympics.

Q1764.name: Reykjavík
facts: The world's northernmost capital of a sovereign state.
Reagan and Gorbachev held a famous summit here in 1986.
Its rocket-shaped Hallgrímskirkja church towers over the city; the Blue Lagoon is nearby.

Q1345.name: Philadelphia
facts: The Declaration of Independence was signed in its Independence Hall in 1776.
Home to the Liberty Bell, and the cheesesteak sandwich.
Rocky Balboa ran up the steps of its Museum of Art in the film Rocky.

Q3820.name: Beirut
facts: Once called the Paris of the Middle East, on the Mediterranean coast.
A massive explosion at its port in August 2020 devastated much of the city.
Pigeon Rocks, two sea arches off its Raouché seafront, are its symbol.

Q1156.name: Mumbai
facts: Formerly called Bombay; home of the Bollywood film industry.
Its dabbawalas deliver home-cooked lunches across the city with near-perfect accuracy.
Its seafront Marine Drive is called the Queen's Necklace; the Taj Mahal Palace hotel is here.

Q1726.name: Munich
facts: Hosts Oktoberfest, the world's largest beer festival.
BMW has its headquarters here; it hosted the 1972 Summer Olympics.
Lies on the Isar River near the Alps; its football club has won six European Cups.

Q5806.name: Mecca
facts: The holiest city in Islam; Muslims around the world face it when praying.
The Kaaba stands in its Great Mosque, the goal of the Hajj pilgrimage.
The Prophet Muhammad was born here around 570.

Q269.name: Tashkent
facts: A major oasis city on the ancient Silk Road.
Rebuilt in Soviet style after a devastating earthquake in 1966.
Its metro has ornate stations; Chorsu Bazaar sits under a giant blue dome.

Q1533.name: Caracas
facts: Simón Bolívar, liberator of much of South America, was born here.
Sits in a mountain valley, separated from the Caribbean by the Ávila mountain.
Cable car rides climb El Ávila, with views of the sea on the other side.

Q2280.name: Minsk
facts: Almost entirely rebuilt in grand Soviet style after World War II.
Ceasefire agreements for the war in eastern Ukraine were signed here in 2014-15.
Lies on the Svislach River; Lee Harvey Oswald lived here in the early 1960s.

Q3838.name: Kinshasa
facts: Lies on a huge river, directly across the water from Brazzaville, another capital.
Formerly named Léopoldville after the Belgian king Leopold II.
Hosted the Rumble in the Jungle boxing match between Ali and Foreman in 1974.

Q216.name: Vilnius
facts: Its baroque Old Town is one of the largest surviving medieval old towns in Northern Europe.
Its bohemian Užupis district declared itself an independent republic as a joke.
Gediminas' Tower overlooks the city where the Vilnia meets the Neris River.

Q2044.name: Florence
facts: Birthplace of the Renaissance, ruled for centuries by the Medici family.
Brunelleschi's dome crowns its cathedral; the Ponte Vecchio spans the Arno.
Michelangelo's David and the Uffizi Gallery are here.

Q1353.name: Delhi
facts: The Mughal Red Fort and the Jama Masjid mosque stand in its old city.
The Qutub Minar, a 73 m brick minaret from the 1190s, is here.
Lies on the Yamuna River; Chandni Chowk market is famous for street food.

Q641.name: Venice
facts: Built on over 100 islands in a lagoon, with canals instead of streets.
Famous for gondolas, St. Mark's Square and the Rialto Bridge.
Marco Polo was born here; it hosts the world's oldest film festival.

Q1461.name: Manila
facts: The Spanish-built walled city of Intramuros is its historic core.
National hero José Rizal was executed here in 1896, in what is now Rizal Park.
Lies on a large bay famous for sunsets, at the mouth of the Pasig River.

Q172.name: Toronto
facts: The CN Tower, once the world's tallest free-standing structure, dominates its skyline.
Lies on the north shore of one of the Great Lakes, near Niagara Falls.
Home to the Hockey Hall of Fame; rapper Drake calls it The 6ix.

Q2634.name: Naples
facts: The birthplace of pizza, including the Margherita.
Mount Vesuvius looms over its bay, with Pompeii's ruins nearby.
Footballer Diego Maradona became a legend playing for its club in the 1980s.

Q5838.name: Kabul
facts: Sits in a valley ringed by the Hindu Kush mountains.
Mughal emperor Babur is buried in its Gardens of Babur.
Khaled Hosseini's novel The Kite Runner is set here.

Q70.name: Bern
facts: Einstein developed his theory of special relativity while living here in 1905.
Its medieval Old Town sits in a tight loop of the Aare River.
Named, by legend, after a bear; live bears still live in a park by the river.

Q31487.name: Kraków
facts: Wawel Castle and its legendary dragon's cave overlook the Vistula River.
Former royal capital; Pope John Paul II was its archbishop.
Oskar Schindler's factory is here; Auschwitz lies about an hour's drive west.

Q612.name: Dubai
facts: Home to the Burj Khalifa, the world's tallest building since 2010.
Famous for the palm-shaped artificial island Palm Jumeirah and the sail-like Burj Al Arab.
Lies on the Persian Gulf; it grew from a pearl-diving village.

Q3894.name: Kampala
facts: Built on seven hills, near the northern shore of Lake Victoria.
The source of the White Nile at Jinja is about 80 km east.
The thatched Kasubi Tombs, burial ground of local kings, are a UNESCO World Heritage Site here.

Q1520.name: Astana
facts: Its Bayterek tower represents a golden egg in a mythical tree of life.
Became the capital in 1997, replacing Almaty; it was renamed Nur-Sultan for a few years.
Khan Shatyr, a giant transparent tent, holds a mall with an indoor beach.

Q1055.name: Hamburg
facts: A major port on the Elbe River, with more bridges than Venice and Amsterdam combined.
The Beatles honed their act in clubs on its Reeperbahn in the early 1960s.
Its wave-roofed Elbphilharmonie concert hall sits on an old harbour warehouse.

Q3692.name: Riyadh
facts: Ibn Saud began founding his kingdom by capturing its Masmak Fort in 1902.
Its Kingdom Centre skyscraper has a famous bottle-opener-shaped gap at the top.
Lies in the middle of the Arabian Peninsula, in the Najd desert plateau.

Q100.name: Boston
facts: Colonists dumped tea into its harbour in the Tea Party of 1773.
Hosts the world's oldest annual marathon; the Red Sox play at Fenway Park.
Harvard University lies just across the Charles River.

Q1563.name: Havana
facts: Famous for its seafront Malecón and colourful 1950s American cars.
Ernest Hemingway lived here; the mojito and daiquiri are linked to its bars.
World-renowned for hand-rolled cigars; it lies on the Florida Straits.

Q1435.name: Zagreb
facts: It sits on the Sava River at the foot of Medvednica mountain.
Home to the Museum of Broken Relationships, filled with mementos of failed love affairs.
St. Mark's Church here has a roof of colourful tiles showing two coats of arms.

Q1867.name: Taipei
facts: Home to a bamboo-shaped skyscraper that was the world's tallest from 2004 to 2010.
The dumpling chain Din Tai Fung began here as a cooking-oil shop in 1958.
The National Palace Museum here holds treasures once kept in Beijing's Forbidden City.

Q3624.name: Addis Ababa
facts: Its name means 'new flower' in Amharic.
The fossil skeleton 'Lucy' is kept in the National Museum here.
It hosts the headquarters of the African Union and sits about 2,350 m above sea level.

Q437.name: Ljubljana
facts: A dragon is the city's symbol, guarding the famous Dragon Bridge.
The Ljubljanica River runs through its old town, crossed by Plečnik's Triple Bridge.
It lies between the Alps and the Adriatic, below a hilltop castle.

Q1953.name: Yerevan
facts: Snow-capped Mount Ararat looms over the city from across the nearby border.
It began as the fortress of Erebuni in 782 BC, making it older than Rome.
It's nicknamed the 'Pink City' for buildings made of rosy volcanic tuff.

Q1519.name: Abu Dhabi
facts: Home to the Sheikh Zayed Grand Mosque with its 82 white domes.
Yas Island here has a Formula 1 circuit and the Ferrari World theme park.
It sits on an island in the Persian Gulf and hosts an outpost of the Louvre.

Q33935.name: Tel Aviv
facts: It was founded in 1909 on sand dunes beside the ancient port of Jaffa.
Its 'White City' of Bauhaus buildings is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
It stretches along the Mediterranean with a long run of busy city beaches.

Q18808.name: Pyongyang
facts: The pyramid-shaped Ryugyong Hotel has towered over it unfinished for decades.
It lies on the Taedong River, beside the Juche Tower.
Its Arch of Triumph was built to be taller than the one in Paris.

Q23556.name: Atlanta
facts: Coca-Cola was invented here by pharmacist John Pemberton in 1886.
Martin Luther King Jr. was born here, and his birth home is a national historic site.
It hosted the 1996 Summer Olympics and is the headquarters of CNN.

Q3561.name: Algiers
facts: Its hillside Casbah is a UNESCO World Heritage Site above the Mediterranean.
It's known as 'the White City' for its whitewashed buildings rising from the bay.
A famous 1966 film about its war of independence was shot in its streets.

Q1362.name: Islamabad
facts: The huge Faisal Mosque stands at the foot of the Margalla Hills here.
It was purpose-built in the 1960s to replace Karachi as the capital.
Its twin city, Rawalpindi, lies right next door.

Q3037.name: Kathmandu
facts: The Swayambhunath stupa here is nicknamed the 'Monkey Temple'.
It's the usual starting point for trekkers and climbers heading for Mount Everest.
A young girl worshipped as the living goddess Kumari lives in a palace in Durbar Square.

Q365.name: Cologne
facts: Its twin-spired Gothic cathedral towers over the Rhine.
A famous light perfume, first made here in the 1700s, is named after the city.
It's famous for its riotous Carnival and its pale Kölsch beer.

Q23430.name: Ulaanbaatar
facts: It's the coldest national capital in the world.
Its name means 'Red Hero'.
The railway between Moscow and Beijing passes through it, crossing the steppe.

Q1335.name: Montevideo
facts: It hosted the first ever FIFA World Cup in 1930, at the Estadio Centenario.
It lies on the Río de la Plata, across the estuary from Buenos Aires.
The famous tango 'La Cumparsita' was composed here in 1916.

Q6602.name: Strasbourg
facts: It's an official seat of the European Parliament.
It lies on the Rhine, facing Kehl in Germany across the river.
The anthem 'La Marseillaise' was composed here in 1792.

Q3551.name: Rabat
facts: The unfinished 12th-century Hassan Tower minaret is its best-known landmark.
It sits on the Atlantic where the Bou Regreg river meets the sea, facing Salé.
The blue-and-white Kasbah of the Udayas overlooks its river mouth.

Q8652.name: Miami
facts: Its South Beach is lined with pastel Art Deco buildings.
Little Havana here is the heart of a huge Cuban exile community.
It's the only major city in its country founded by a woman, Julia Tuttle.

Q456.name: Lyon
facts: It sits where the Rhône and Saône rivers meet.
The Lumière brothers invented the cinematograph and showed early films here.
Each December the Festival of Lights fills it with illuminations; it's a famed food capital.

Q1348.name: Kolkata
facts: The Howrah Bridge spans the Hooghly River here.
Mother Teresa founded her Missionaries of Charity here.
It was the capital of the British Raj until 1911, and Rabindranath Tagore was born here.

Q3926.name: Pretoria
facts: It's called the 'Jacaranda City' for the purple trees that bloom each spring.
Nelson Mandela was inaugurated as president at its Union Buildings in 1994.
It's named after the Voortrekker leader Andries Pretorius.

Q8660.name: Karachi
facts: Muhammad Ali Jinnah was born here, and his white marble mausoleum is a landmark.
It's a huge port city on the Arabian Sea, near the Indus River delta.
It was the nation's first capital, before Islamabad was built.

Q23768.name: Las Vegas
facts: Its famous Strip of mega-casinos is nicknamed 'Sin City'.
It sits in the Mojave Desert, not far from the Hoover Dam.
Elvis Presley married Priscilla here in 1967.

Q3579.name: Tripoli
facts: Its name comes from the Greek for 'three cities'.
The 'shores of' it in the US Marines' Hymn recall the First Barbary War.
A Roman arch of Marcus Aurelius stands near its Red Castle on the Mediterranean.

Q340.name: Montreal
facts: It's built on an island in the St. Lawrence River, around Mount Royal.
It hosted Expo 67 and the 1976 Summer Olympics.
It's famous for wood-fired bagels, smoked meat sandwiches and poutine.

Q1794.name: Frankfurt
facts: Its skyscraper skyline on the Main river earned it the nickname 'Mainhattan'.
Johann Wolfgang von Goethe was born here in 1749.
It's home to the European Central Bank and the world's largest book fair.

Q23661.name: Wellington
facts: It's often called the windiest city in the world, on the shore of Cook Strait.
Weta studios made 'The Lord of the Rings' here, earning it the nickname 'Wellywood'.
Its parliament building is nicknamed 'The Beehive'.

Q3861.name: Doha
facts: It was the centre of the 2022 FIFA World Cup.
Its Museum of Islamic Art was designed by I. M. Pei.
It's the home of the Al Jazeera news network, on a curving Persian Gulf corniche.

Q5083.name: Seattle
facts: The Space Needle was built here for the 1962 World's Fair.
The first Starbucks opened at its Pike Place Market in 1971.
It lies on Puget Sound, with Mount Rainier on the horizon, and gave the world grunge.

Q87.name: Alexandria
facts: It was founded by Alexander the Great in 331 BC.
Its ancient Lighthouse of Pharos was one of the Seven Wonders of the World.
It sits on the Mediterranean at the western edge of the Nile Delta.

Q3856.name: Nicosia
facts: It's the last divided capital in Europe, split by a UN-patrolled Green Line.
Its old town is ringed by star-shaped Venetian walls with 11 bastions.
It lies inland on a plain between two mountain ranges, on an island in the Mediterranean.

Q23436.name: Edinburgh
facts: Its castle sits on an extinct volcano, near the hill called Arthur's Seat.
Every August it hosts the Fringe, the world's largest arts festival.
J. K. Rowling wrote much of the early Harry Potter books in its cafés.

Q2900.name: Quito
facts: It sits about 2,850 m up on the slopes of Pichincha volcano.
The 'Middle of the World' monument marks the equator just north of the city.
In 1978 its old town was among the first places named UNESCO World Heritage Sites.

Q16555.name: Houston
facts: NASA's Mission Control is here; Apollo 13 radioed it with 'we've had a problem'.
It's a world capital of the oil industry, linked to Galveston Bay by a ship channel.
Its MLB team is the Astros and its NBA team the Rockets, fitting for a space city.

Q9022.name: Guadalajara
facts: It's considered the birthplace of mariachi music.
The town of Tequila, home of the famous spirit, is about an hour away.
The Hospicio Cabañas here is covered in murals by José Clemente Orozco.

Q495.name: Turin
facts: Fiat was founded here in 1899, and it's home to Juventus football club.
A linen cloth said to be the burial shroud of Jesus is kept in its cathedral.
It sits on the Po River with the Alps behind it, and hosted the 2006 Winter Olympics.

Q43387.name: Edirne
facts: The Selimiye Mosque here is considered Mimar Sinan's masterpiece.
It hosts Kırkpınar, an oil-wrestling tournament held since the 1300s.
Once called Adrianople after Emperor Hadrian, it sits near the Greek and Bulgarian borders.

Q1449.name: Genoa
facts: Christopher Columbus was born here.
It's the home of pesto and focaccia, and the word 'jeans' comes from its name.
It's a great port on the Ligurian Sea, guarded by the Lanterna lighthouse.

Q384.name: Skopje
facts: Mother Teresa was born here in 1910.
An old stone bridge crosses the Vardar River into its Ottoman-era bazaar.
A 1963 earthquake destroyed much of it; it's now dotted with giant statues.

Q23800.name: Valletta
facts: The Knights of St John built it after the Great Siege of 1565.
St John's Co-Cathedral here holds Caravaggio's 'The Beheading of Saint John'.
It's the smallest capital in the EU, overlooking the Grand Harbour.

Q71.name: Geneva
facts: Its Jet d'Eau fountain shoots water 140 m into the air from Lac Léman.
The Red Cross was founded here, and it hosts the UN's European headquarters.
The CERN particle physics lab lies on its outskirts, near the border.

Q3761.name: Accra
facts: It lies on the Gulf of Guinea coast of West Africa.
Craftsmen here build 'fantasy coffins' shaped like fish, cars or even shoes.
Kwame Nkrumah's mausoleum and the Black Star Gate stand here.

Q23438.name: Ashgabat
facts: It holds the Guinness record for the most white marble buildings.
It lies between the Karakum Desert and the Kopetdag mountains, near Iran.
Almost the whole city was flattened by an earthquake in 1948.

Q18125.name: Manchester
facts: Its cotton mills made it the world's first industrial city, 'Cottonopolis'.
Ernest Rutherford split the atom here, and the first stored-program computer ran here.
It's home to two giant football clubs, at Old Trafford and the Etihad Stadium.

Q35765.name: Osaka
facts: Called 'the nation's kitchen', it's famous for takoyaki and okonomiyaki.
Its Dōtonbori canal district is known for the giant Glico running-man sign.
It hosted World Expos in 1970 and 2025, and has a castle built by Toyotomi Hideyoshi.

Q24639.name: Vancouver
facts: Its huge Stanley Park juts out between the harbour and English Bay.
It hosted the 2010 Winter Olympics.
Greenpeace was founded here in 1971, and film crews call it 'Hollywood North'.

Q3787.name: Abuja
facts: It replaced Lagos as the national capital in 1991.
The giant granite monolith Aso Rock rises behind its government buildings.
It's a planned city, built at the geographic centre of its country.

Q3805.name: Amman
facts: Its hilltop Citadel holds the ruins of a Roman Temple of Hercules.
In Roman times it was called Philadelphia, and its Roman theatre still stands.
It's about an hour's drive from the Dead Sea.

Q1479.name: Bordeaux
facts: It's the world-famous wine capital, on the Garonne River.
The Place de la Bourse is mirrored in the world's largest reflecting pool.
It's the home of the canelé pastry, and its curving riverfront is the 'Port of the Moon'.

Q8673.name: Lagos
facts: Its name is Portuguese for 'lakes', after its lagoon on the Gulf of Guinea.
Fela Kuti created Afrobeat here, and it's the home of Nollywood.
It was the national capital until Abuja took over in 1991.

Q2471.name: Sanaa
facts: Its old city of mud-brick tower houses trimmed with white gypsum is a UNESCO site.
It's one of the world's highest capitals, at about 2,300 m.
Legend says it was founded by Shem, son of Noah.

Q36600.name: The Hague
facts: The International Court of Justice sits in its Peace Palace.
Vermeer's 'Girl with a Pearl Earring' hangs in its Mauritshuis museum.
It's the seat of government but not the capital; its beach resort is Scheveningen.

Q83285.name: Durrës
facts: Founded by Greeks in 627 BC as Epidamnos, it was later the Roman Dyrrachium.
It has the largest Roman amphitheatre in the Balkans.
It's the main port on its country's Adriatic coast.

Q16554.name: Denver
facts: It's the 'Mile High City'; one step of its Capitol is exactly a mile up.
It sits on the plains at the foot of the Rocky Mountains.
It began as a gold-rush town in 1858 and still mints the nation's coins.

Q24826.name: Liverpool
facts: The Beatles formed here and played the Cavern Club.
It sits on the River Mersey, and the Titanic was registered here.
It's home to Anfield and Goodison Park, and the Grand National is run nearby.

Q3572.name: Tunis
facts: The ruins of ancient Carthage are in its suburbs.
The Bardo Museum here has one of the world's finest collections of Roman mosaics.
The blue-and-white village of Sidi Bou Said overlooks its Mediterranean gulf.

Q18094.name: Honolulu
facts: Waikiki Beach and Diamond Head crater are here.
Pearl Harbor, attacked in 1941, is just west of the city.
Barack Obama was born here; ʻIolani Palace is the only royal palace in its country.

Q72.name: Zurich
facts: The Dada art movement was born here at the Cabaret Voltaire in 1916.
It sits where the Limmat River flows out of a long Alpine lake.
FIFA has its headquarters here, and Einstein studied at its ETH university.

Q34647.name: Johannesburg
facts: It was founded in an 1886 gold rush, and its Zulu name eGoli means 'place of gold'.
Soweto's Vilakazi Street was home to both Nelson Mandela and Desmond Tutu.
It hosted the 2010 FIFA World Cup final at Soccer City.

Q33959.name: Nice
facts: Its Promenade des Anglais curves along the Baie des Anges.
It's the main city of the Côte d'Azur, a short drive from Monaco.
Matisse lived here, and its famous chickpea pancake is called socca.

Q5776.name: Bethlehem
facts: The Church of the Nativity marks the traditional birthplace of Jesus.
It's the hometown of King David in the Bible.
Banksy opened the Walled Off Hotel here, beside the West Bank barrier.

Q16556.name: Phoenix
facts: It's named after the mythical bird, rising from the ruins of Hohokam canals.
It sits in the Sonoran Desert, in the 'Valley of the Sun', among saguaro cacti.
Camelback Mountain rises in the middle of its sprawl.

Q2449.name: Mogadishu
facts: The 1993 'Black Hawk Down' battle took place here.
It's an old Indian Ocean trading port that Ibn Battuta visited in 1331.
Its Lido Beach is a popular seaside spot.

Q34404.name: New Orleans
facts: It's the birthplace of jazz and of Louis Armstrong.
Its Mardi Gras is famous, centred on the French Quarter by the Mississippi.
Hurricane Katrina flooded most of the city in 2005; try its beignets and gumbo.

Q12439.name: Detroit
facts: It's the 'Motor City', where Henry Ford made the Model T.
Berry Gordy founded the Motown record label here in 1959.
Across its river lies Windsor, Canada, which is actually to the south.

Q21197.name: Chișinău
facts: Pushkin lived here in exile in the early 1820s.
Its Russian-era name was Kishinev.
The underground wine cellars at nearby Cricova stretch for over 100 km.

Q16557.name: Dallas
facts: President John F. Kennedy was assassinated at Dealey Plaza here in 1963.
Jack Kilby invented the integrated circuit here in 1958.
The frozen margarita machine was invented here, and its State Fair has a giant 'Big Tex'.

Q1850.name: Phnom Penh
facts: It stands where the Tonlé Sap river meets the Mekong.
The Royal Palace and Silver Pagoda line its riverfront.
The Khmer Rouge emptied the city in 1975; Tuol Sleng prison is now a museum.

Q4093.name: Glasgow
facts: Shipyards on the River Clyde here built the Queen Mary and the QE2.
Its fierce Celtic-Rangers football rivalry is known as the Old Firm.
Charles Rennie Mackintosh designed its famous School of Art.

Q34820.name: Santo Domingo
facts: Founded in 1496, it's the oldest permanent European city in the Americas.
Its Colonial Zone has the first cathedral built in the Americas.
It sits on the Caribbean at the mouth of the Ozama River; merengue rules here.

Q16572.name: Guangzhou
facts: It was the old trading port Europeans called Canton, home of the Canton Fair.
It's the heartland of Cantonese cuisine and dim sum, on the Pearl River.
The slender, twisting Canton Tower dominates its skyline.

Q1963.name: Khartoum
facts: The Blue Nile and the White Nile meet here.
General Gordon was killed here in 1885 during a siege by the Mahdi's forces.
Its name is often said to mean 'elephant's trunk', after the shape of the river fork.

Q3183.name: Perth
facts: It's often called the most isolated big city in the world, on the Indian Ocean.
It lies on the Swan River, named for its black swans.
Rottnest Island, home of the smiling quokka, lies just offshore.

Q3921.name: Harare
facts: It was called Salisbury until 1982.
A rocky hill called the Kopje overlooks the city centre.
Its streets turn purple with blooming jacarandas each spring.

Q1842.name: Luxembourg
facts: The Bock Casemates are miles of tunnels carved into its cliffs.
It sits above the deep gorges of the Alzette and Pétrusse rivers.
It hosts the EU's Court of Justice, close to the Belgian, French and German borders.

Q803.name: Utrecht
facts: Its Dom Tower is the tallest church tower in the country.
Dick Bruna, creator of Miffy, lived and worked here.
It has the world's largest bicycle parking garage, beside the central station.

Q5823.name: Ceuta
facts: It sits on the Strait of Gibraltar, facing the Rock of Gibraltar.
Its Monte Hacho is one candidate for the southern Pillar of Hercules.
It's a small enclave on the coast of Africa, bordered by Morocco.

Q16559.name: Austin
facts: It calls itself the 'Live Music Capital of the World' and hosts SXSW.
Over a million bats emerge each summer evening from its Congress Avenue Bridge.
Michael Dell started Dell computers in a university dorm room here.

Q7880.name: Toulouse
facts: Airbus is headquartered here, and the Concorde was assembled here.
It's called 'La Ville Rose' for its pinkish brick buildings.
It lies on the Garonne and the Canal du Midi, and is famous for cassoulet.

Q2256.name: Birmingham
facts: Cadbury chocolate is made at Bournville here.
It's said to have more miles of canals than Venice.
Black Sabbath formed here, and 'Peaky Blinders' is set here.

Q3718.name: Dakar
facts: It's on the westernmost point of mainland Africa, on the Cap-Vert peninsula.
For decades the famous desert rally that started in Paris finished here.
The African Renaissance Monument here is taller than the Statue of Liberty.

Q3306.name: Panama City
facts: It sits at the Pacific end of the famous canal linking two oceans.
The pirate Henry Morgan sacked the original city in 1671; its ruins still stand.
Frank Gehry designed its brightly coloured Biomuseo.

Q12892.name: Antwerp
facts: It's the world's diamond capital, with a famous diamond district.
Painter Peter Paul Rubens lived here, and his house is a museum.
It's one of Europe's biggest ports, on the Scheldt river.

Q1355.name: Bengaluru
facts: It's known as the country's 'Silicon Valley', home of Infosys and many tech firms.
It's nicknamed the 'Garden City', with Lalbagh and Cubbon Park.
It sits on a high plateau, which gives it a mild climate year-round.

Q9361.name: Bishkek
facts: From 1926 to 1991 it was named Frunze, after a Red Army commander born here.
The snowy Ala-Too mountains rise just south of the city.
Its name is said to come from a churn used to make kumis, fermented mare's milk.

Q1799.name: Wrocław
facts: Hundreds of little bronze dwarf statues are hidden around its streets.
It was called Breslau and sits on the Oder River, with over 100 bridges.
Its Centennial Hall is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

Q18013.name: Sacramento
facts: It stands where the American River flows into the state's longest river.
Gold was found at nearby Sutter's Mill in 1848, sparking a famous gold rush.
It was the western end of the Pony Express.

Q5831.name: Melilla
facts: It's a small enclave on the North African coast, bordered by Morocco.
Francisco Franco's 1936 uprising, which began a civil war, started here.
It has a walled old fortress town and many modernist buildings by Enrique Nieto.

Q16552.name: San Diego
facts: Its Balboa Park houses one of the world's most famous zoos.
It hosts Comic-Con every summer and is home port to much of the Pacific Fleet.
It sits on the Pacific right next to the border with Tijuana.

Q3826.name: Muscat
facts: The Sultan Qaboos Grand Mosque here has one of the world's largest hand-woven carpets.
Its harbour is guarded by the twin 16th-century forts of Al Jalali and Al Mirani.
It's squeezed between the Hajar Mountains and the sea, near the Strait of Hormuz.

Q34932.name: Brisbane
facts: It will host the 2032 Summer Olympics.
The Story Bridge crosses the winding river that runs through its centre.
Lone Pine Koala Sanctuary here is the world's oldest koala sanctuary.

Q1731.name: Dresden
facts: Its Frauenkirche was rebuilt after the 1945 firebombing.
It's the setting of Kurt Vonnegut's 'Slaughterhouse-Five'.
It's called 'Florence on the Elbe' and is famous for Christmas Stollen.

Q374365.name: Jeddah
facts: It's the gateway for pilgrims heading to Mecca for the Hajj.
King Fahd's Fountain here shoots water over 250 m high into the Red Sea air.
Its old Al-Balad district is built of coral stone.

Q36036.name: Lviv
facts: Its symbol is the lion, after Prince Lev, son of its founder King Danylo.
It's famous for its coffee houses and chocolate makers.
It was called Lemberg and Lwów; Leopold von Sacher-Masoch was born here.

Q3897.name: Luanda
facts: It lies on the Atlantic coast of southern Africa.
Founded by the Portuguese in 1576, it's watched over by the Fortress of São Miguel.
A long sandy spit called the Ilha shelters its bay.

Q11725.name: Chongqing
facts: It sits where the Jialing River joins the Yangtze; Three Gorges cruises start here.
It's famous for fiery Sichuan-style hot pot.
Its Liziba station has a monorail running straight through an apartment building.

Q34713.name: Salzburg
facts: Mozart was born here in 1756.
'The Sound of Music' was filmed here.
Its name means 'salt castle', and a huge medieval fortress overlooks the Salzach River.

Q5092.name: Baltimore
facts: Fort McHenry's defence here in 1814 inspired 'The Star-Spangled Banner'.
Its NFL team, the Ravens, is named after Edgar Allan Poe's poem; Poe died here.
Its Inner Harbor opens onto Chesapeake Bay, and it's famous for crab cakes.

Q10686.name: Belfast
facts: The Titanic was built here at the Harland & Wolff shipyard.
Two giant yellow cranes, Samson and Goliath, dominate its skyline.
C. S. Lewis was born here; it lies where the River Lagan meets the sea.

Q1352.name: Chennai
facts: Marina Beach here is one of the longest urban beaches in the world.
It sits on the Bay of Bengal and is the home of the Tamil film industry.
Fort St. George, founded here in 1639, was the first English fortress on the subcontinent.

Q23337.name: Salt Lake City
facts: Worldwide headquarters of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints, centred on Temple Square.
It hosted the 2002 Winter Olympics.
It sits beneath the Wasatch Range, near a vast salty lake left over from ancient Lake Bonneville.

Q1022.name: Stuttgart
facts: Mercedes-Benz and Porsche are both headquartered here, each with its own museum.
It lies in a valley on the Neckar river, surrounded by vineyards.
Its TV tower, opened in 1956, was the world's first made of reinforced concrete.

Q2933.name: Asunción
facts: Founded in 1537, it is one of the oldest cities in South America, nicknamed the 'Mother of Cities'.
It lies on a river opposite Argentina, just upstream of where the Pilcomayo joins it.
Its Pantheon of the Heroes holds the remains of national war heroes and presidents.

Q23197.name: Nashville
facts: Known as 'Music City', it is the home of the Grand Ole Opry and country music.
It has a full-scale replica of the Parthenon of Athens.
It sits on the Cumberland River and is famous for spicy hot chicken.

Q2090.name: Nuremberg
facts: Host of the Nazi party rallies and, after WWII, the famous war crimes trials.
Painter Albrecht Dürer was born and worked here.
Famed for its Christmas market, Lebkuchen gingerbread and finger-sized bratwurst.

Q1792.name: Gdańsk
facts: The Solidarity movement led by Lech Wałęsa was born in its shipyard in 1980.
WWII began here in 1939 when the Westerplatte peninsula was shelled.
Historically known as Danzig, it is a Baltic port famous for amber and the Neptune Fountain.

Q11739.name: Lahore
facts: Home to the vast Badshahi Mosque and the Mughal-era Shalimar Gardens.
It lies on the Ravi River, close to the Wagah border crossing with India.
Often called the cultural heart of its country, it hosts the Data Darbar shrine.

Q6346.name: Indianapolis
facts: Its Motor Speedway hosts a famous 500-mile race every Memorial Day weekend.
It hosts the Indy 500, the world's biggest single-day sporting event.
Home of the NFL's Colts and the NBA's Pacers.

Q5753.name: Samarkand
facts: Its Registan square is framed by three tiled madrasas.
A great Silk Road city, it was Timur's (Tamerlane's) capital; his tomb is the Gur-e-Amir.
Astronomer-king Ulugh Beg built a huge observatory here in the 1420s.

Q900.name: Kazan
facts: Its Kremlin holds both an Orthodox cathedral and the blue-domed Qolsharif Mosque.
It sits on the Volga, where a small tributary joins it from the north.
Ivan the Terrible's capture of the city in 1552 was celebrated by building St Basil's Cathedral.

Q1070.name: Ahmedabad
facts: Gandhi's Sabarmati Ashram, starting point of the 1930 Salt March, is here.
It has the world's largest cricket stadium, named after Narendra Modi.
In 2017 its old walled city became its country's first UNESCO World Heritage City.

Q16567.name: Columbus
facts: Named after the explorer who sailed to the Americas in 1492.
The fast-food chain Wendy's opened its first restaurant here in 1969.
It sits where the Scioto and Olentangy rivers meet.

Q17151.name: Thessaloniki
facts: Its seafront landmark is the White Tower, on the Thermaic Gulf.
Founded around 315 BC and named after Alexander the Great's half-sister.
Mustafa Kemal Atatürk was born here in 1881.

Q3935.name: Windhoek
facts: It sits on a central highland plateau between the Namib and Kalahari deserts.
Its landmark Christuskirche dates from the German colonial era.
It gives its name to a well-known lager brewed here to the old German purity law.

Q1829.name: Kaliningrad
facts: Formerly Königsberg, home of philosopher Immanuel Kant.
Its seven bridges inspired Euler's famous problem that founded graph theory.
A Baltic exclave between Poland and Lithuania, and a world centre of amber mining.

Q35381.name: Colombo
facts: Its seafront promenade, Galle Face Green, faces the Indian Ocean.
The Lotus Tower, shaped like a lotus bud, is one of South Asia's tallest structures.
A port long ruled by the Portuguese, Dutch and British, near the mouth of the Kelani River.

Q5112.name: Adelaide
facts: Planned by Colonel William Light, with a grid centre ringed by parklands.
Nicknamed the 'City of Churches', it hosts one of the world's largest Fringe festivals.
The Barossa Valley wine region lies just to its north-east.

Q23564.name: Podgorica
facts: It was called Titograd from 1946 to 1992, after Yugoslav leader Tito.
It stands where the Ribnica meets the Morača river.
Skadar Lake, the largest lake in the Balkans, lies just to the south.

Q37100.name: Auckland
facts: Built on a volcanic field of around 50 volcanoes, including Rangitoto island.
Nicknamed the 'City of Sails', it lies on a narrow isthmus between two harbours.
Its Sky Tower is the tallest freestanding structure in the Southern Hemisphere.

Q36091.name: Minneapolis
facts: Twin Cities partner of St Paul, on the Mississippi at St Anthony Falls.
Once the flour-milling capital of the world; General Mills and Pillsbury began here.
Home city of the musician Prince, and of the giant 'Spoonbridge and Cherry' sculpture.

Q1342.name: Pittsburgh
facts: The Allegheny and Monongahela rivers meet here to form the Ohio River.
Nicknamed 'Steel City', it is also called the 'City of Bridges' for its hundreds of spans.
Andy Warhol was born here, and Heinz ketchup has been made here since the 1800s.

Q2656.name: Palermo
facts: Its Teatro Massimo, one of Europe's largest opera houses, features in The Godfather Part III.
Famed for Arab-Norman architecture and street food like arancine and panelle.
Its Capuchin Catacombs hold thousands of mummified bodies.

Q1491.name: La Paz
facts: At about 3,600 m, it is the world's highest seat of government.
It has the world's largest urban cable-car network, Mi Teleférico.
Snow-capped Illimani towers over the city, and Lake Titicaca is nearby.

Q1361.name: Hyderabad
facts: Its icon is the 16th-century Charminar, a four-minaret monument.
Famous for its biryani and pearls, and for the nearby Golconda Fort.
Home to Ramoji Film City, one of the world's largest film studio complexes.

Q7903.name: Casablanca
facts: Gave its name to the 1942 film starring Humphrey Bogart and Ingrid Bergman.
The Hassan II Mosque stands partly over the Atlantic, with a towering minaret.
Its name means 'white house' in Spanish.

Q10690.name: Cardiff
facts: Its Principality Stadium was one of the first in its country with a retractable roof.
Children's author Roald Dahl was born here in 1916.
Once the world's biggest coal-exporting port, it is now a main filming base of Doctor Who.

Q2079.name: Leipzig
facts: J. S. Bach was cantor of St Thomas Church here and is buried there.
Its 1989 Monday demonstrations helped bring down the Berlin Wall.
The huge Monument to the Battle of the Nations recalls Napoleon's 1813 defeat here.

Q34692.name: Kingston
facts: Birthplace of reggae culture in Trench Town; Bob Marley's former home is a museum here.
Pirate haven Port Royal, partly sunk by an earthquake in 1692, lies across its harbour.
The coffee-growing Blue Mountains rise behind the city.

Q4361.name: Curitiba
facts: A pioneer of bus rapid transit, famous for its glass tube bus stations.
Its Wire Opera House is built of steel tubes in a former quarry.
Its Botanical Garden greenhouse, of glass and iron, is a city symbol.

Q1718.name: Düsseldorf
facts: Its luxury shopping street, the Königsallee, runs beside a canal.
Famous for its dark Altbier and its Rhine-side old town 'longest bar in the world'.
The electronic band Kraftwerk was formed here.

Q34664.name: Hiroshima
facts: Destroyed by the first atomic bomb used in war, on 6 August 1945.
Its Peace Memorial Park holds the skeletal A-Bomb Dome.
Famous for its layered style of okonomiyaki; the floating torii of Miyajima is nearby.

Q1874.name: Odesa
facts: Its Potemkin Stairs became famous from Eisenstein's film Battleship Potemkin.
A Black Sea port founded by Catherine the Great's decree in 1794.
Its ornate Opera and Ballet Theatre is one of the city's great landmarks.

Q959.name: Vladivostok
facts: The eastern terminus of the Trans-Siberian Railway.
Home port of the Pacific Fleet, on the Golden Horn Bay of the Sea of Japan.
Its name means roughly 'Ruler of the East'.

Q11746.name: Wuhan
facts: The Yangtze and Han rivers meet here, splitting it into three historic towns.
The 1911 Wuchang Uprising here sparked the revolution that ended imperial rule.
COVID-19 was first identified here in late 2019; it is also famed for hot dry noodles.

Q975.name: San Antonio
facts: Home to the Alamo, site of the 1836 siege.
Its River Walk is a network of paths along a river below street level.
Home of the NBA's Spurs; its Spanish missions are a World Heritage Site.

Q6106.name: Portland
facts: It lies where the Willamette meets the Columbia, with Mount Hood on the skyline.
Its name was chosen by a coin toss; the loser's choice was Boston.
Home to Powell's, one of the world's largest independent bookstores.

Q101625.name: Marrakech
facts: Its main square, Jemaa el-Fnaa, fills with storytellers, snake charmers and food stalls.
Nicknamed the 'Red City', it sits below the snowy High Atlas Mountains.
The Majorelle Garden, once owned by Yves Saint Laurent, is here.

Q33986.name: Valparaíso
facts: Its steep hills are climbed by historic funiculars and lined with colourful houses.
Poet Pablo Neruda's house La Sebastiana overlooks the bay.
Its National Congress sits here, away from the capital.

Q35484.name: Medina
facts: Home of the Prophet's Mosque, which contains the tomb of Muhammad.
Muhammad's migration here in 622, the Hijra, marks year one of the Islamic calendar.
Its ancient name was Yathrib; it holds the Quba Mosque, said to be Islam's first.

Q36312.name: Calgary
facts: Hosts the Stampede, a huge annual rodeo and festival.
It hosted the 1988 Winter Olympics.
It sits on the Bow River, a short drive east of the Rocky Mountains and Banff.

Q7525.name: Sevastopol
facts: A naval port on the Black Sea, long home of the Black Sea Fleet.
Besieged for nearly a year in 1854-55 by British, French and Ottoman forces.
The ancient Greek city of Chersonesus lies within its limits.

Q35493.name: Almaty
facts: Formerly Alma-Ata, it lies at the foot of the Trans-Ili Alatau mountains.
The region is thought to be the birthplace of the wild apple.
Medeu, a high-altitude ice rink in the mountains above, is famous for speed-skating records.

Q25270.name: Pristina
facts: Its 'Newborn' monument was unveiled on the day of independence in 2008.
Its National Library is known for its unusual domes and metal-mesh facade.
A boulevard here is named after Bill Clinton, with a statue of him.

Q37836.name: Milwaukee
facts: Harley-Davidson was founded and is headquartered here.
Famous for beer: Miller, Pabst and Schlitz all brewed here.
On Lake Michigan, its Calatrava-designed art museum has wing-like sunshades.

Q2467.name: Nassau
facts: Once a pirate republic, a base for Blackbeard in the early 1700s.
On New Providence island, linked by bridge to Paradise Island's Atlantis resort.
Famous for its Junkanoo street parades at Christmas and New Year.

Q3859.name: Kigali
facts: Its memorial commemorates the victims of the 1994 genocide against the Tutsi.
Spread across many green hills, it is often called one of Africa's cleanest cities.
Its country banned plastic bags in 2008, and residents join monthly community clean-ups.

Q16553.name: San Jose
facts: Calls itself the 'Capital of Silicon Valley'; Cisco, Adobe and eBay are based here.
The labyrinthine Winchester Mystery House is a famous oddity here.
Home of the NHL's Sharks; it lies at the southern end of San Francisco Bay.

Q38022.name: St. Louis
facts: Its Gateway Arch, 192 m tall, is the world's tallest arch.
It hosted the 1904 World's Fair and Summer Olympics.
Anheuser-Busch, maker of Budweiser, was founded here, on the Mississippi just below a great river confluence.

Q3777.name: Ouagadougou
facts: Hosts FESPACO, Africa's largest film festival, every two years.
Historically the seat of the Mossi Empire's Mogho Naba king.
The revolutionary leader Thomas Sankara is buried here.

Q3751.name: Praia
facts: It sits on the southern coast of Santiago, an Atlantic island.
Its name means 'beach' in Portuguese.
Nearby Cidade Velha was the first European colonial town in the tropics.

Q34370.name: Rotterdam
facts: Its port is the largest in Europe, near where the Rhine and Maas reach the North Sea.
The scholar Erasmus was born here; its Erasmus Bridge is nicknamed 'The Swan'.
Rebuilt after 1940 bombing, it is famed for modern architecture like the Cube Houses and Markthal.

Q9427.name: Timbuktu
facts: Long a byword for the remotest place on Earth, as in 'from here to ...'.
Near the Niger River, it holds the mud-brick Djinguereber Mosque and ancient manuscripts.
It grew rich on Saharan trade under the Mali Empire of Mansa Musa.

Q66485.name: Jaipur
facts: Nicknamed the 'Pink City' for its painted old town.
Its Hawa Mahal, a honeycomb palace facade, has 953 small windows.
Amber Fort and the Jantar Mantar observatory are among its sights.

Q25287.name: Gothenburg
facts: Volvo was founded here in 1927 and is still based here.
Home of Liseberg, one of Scandinavia's largest amusement parks.
It lies where the Göta älv river meets the Kattegat sea.

Q23154.name: Bristol
facts: Brunel's Clifton Suspension Bridge spans the Avon Gorge here.
Street artist Banksy and trip-hop band Massive Attack come from here.
Aardman Animations, creators of Wallace and Gromit, are based here.

Q34863.name: Oklahoma City
facts: Founded in a single day during the Land Run of 1889.
The world's first parking meter was installed here in 1935.
Home of the NBA's Thunder and the National Cowboy and Western Heritage Museum.

Q3915.name: Antananarivo
facts: The royal palace complex, the Rova, crowns the highest hill.
Its name means 'City of the Thousand', after the soldiers said to guard it.
Lake Anosy, ringed by purple jacaranda trees, lies at its heart.

Q3882.name: Manama
facts: The Gulf island state's capital was long a centre of pearl diving.
The King Fahd Causeway links its island to Saudi Arabia.
Its World Trade Center has three giant wind turbines between its twin towers.

Q37701.name: Bloemfontein
facts: J. R. R. Tolkien was born here in 1892.
Its name is often translated as 'fountain of flowers'; it is nicknamed the 'City of Roses'.
It is its country's judicial capital, and the ANC was founded here in 1912.

Q38283.name: Yokohama
facts: Its Chinatown is the largest in East Asia outside China.
It hosted the 2002 FIFA World Cup final, on Tokyo Bay.
It has a Cup Noodles Museum and the Minato Mirai waterfront with its Landmark Tower.

Q3642.name: Asmara
facts: Famous for its Italian-era modernist buildings, such as the Fiat Tagliero station.
Its architecture became a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2017.
It sits about 2,300 m up on a highland plateau above the Red Sea coast.

Q34804.name: Albuquerque
facts: Hosts the International Balloon Fiesta, the world's largest hot-air balloon festival.
The TV series Breaking Bad was set and filmed here.
Microsoft was founded here in 1975; Route 66 and the Rio Grande cross the city.

Q914.name: Volgograd
facts: Formerly Stalingrad, it was the site of the decisive WWII battle of 1942-43.
'The Motherland Calls', a giant sword-raising statue, stands on Mamayev Kurgan.
It stretches for many kilometres along the west bank of the Volga.

Q1017.name: Aachen
facts: Charlemagne's favourite residence; he is buried in its cathedral.
It lies right at the meeting point with Belgium and the Netherlands.
Known for its hot springs, Printen gingerbread and the CHIO equestrian show.

Q3748.name: Monrovia
facts: Named after US President James Monroe.
Founded in 1822 on Cape Mesurado as a settlement for freed African-American slaves.
Football star turned president George Weah grew up here.

Q9326.name: Vientiane
facts: It lies on the Mekong, facing Thailand across the river.
Its golden stupa, Pha That Luang, is the national symbol.
Its Patuxai arch was reportedly built with US cement meant for an airport runway.

Q16563.name: Memphis
facts: Elvis Presley's mansion Graceland and Sun Studio are here.
Martin Luther King Jr. was assassinated at its Lorraine Motel in 1968.
Home of Beale Street blues and FedEx; it is named after an ancient Egyptian city.

Q16568.name: Jacksonville
facts: By land area it is the largest city in its country outside Alaska.
The St. Johns River winds through it to the Atlantic.
Home of the NFL's Jaguars; the band Lynyrd Skynyrd formed here.

Q1715.name: Hanover
facts: Its electors became Britain's kings, starting with George I in 1714.
It hosts the Hannover Messe, one of the world's largest industrial trade fairs, and hosted Expo 2000.
Its baroque Herrenhausen Gardens are among Europe's finest; it lies on the Leine river.

Q29445.name: Juneau
facts: It is a state capital that cannot be reached by road from the rest of the continent.
The Mendenhall Glacier lies within the city limits.
Founded in a gold rush in 1880, it is a popular cruise stop on the Inside Passage.

Q37951.name: Sapporo
facts: Its Snow Festival fills Odori Park with giant ice and snow sculptures every February.
It hosted the 1972 Winter Olympics, the first held in Asia.
A city laid out on a grid, famous for miso ramen and its namesake beer.

Q39450.name: Anchorage
facts: The Iditarod sled dog race has its ceremonial start here.
It was struck by the magnitude 9.2 Good Friday earthquake of 1964.
It sits on Cook Inlet, and moose often wander its streets.

Q15174.name: Shenzhen
facts: A fishing area turned into its country's first special economic zone in 1980.
Huawei, Tencent, BYD and DJI are all headquartered here.
It sits directly north of Hong Kong, across a river border.

Q586.name: Bonn
facts: Ludwig van Beethoven was born here in 1770.
It served as the Cold War-era seat of government from 1949 until reunification in 1990.
Gummy bear maker Haribo was founded here; it sits on the Rhine.

Q37320.name: Cleveland
facts: Home of the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame on Lake Erie.
The Cuyahoga River here famously caught fire in 1969.
The house from the film A Christmas Story is a tourist attraction here.

Q36526.name: Port Moresby
facts: Named after Captain John Moresby, who charted the harbour in 1873.
It lies on the southern coast of the island of New Guinea, facing the Coral Sea.
Its Hanuabada village is famous for houses built on stilts over the water.

Q2145.name: Quebec City
facts: The Château Frontenac hotel looms over its walled old town.
Founded by Samuel de Champlain in 1608 on the St. Lawrence River.
Its Winter Carnival is hosted by a snowman mascot called Bonhomme.

Q34217.name: Oxford
facts: Home of the oldest university in the English-speaking world.
Lewis Carroll wrote Alice's Adventures in Wonderland here; Tolkien wrote much of his work here.
Christ Church college's hall inspired Hogwarts in the Harry Potter films.

Q34261.name: Port-au-Prince
facts: Much of it was destroyed in the devastating earthquake of January 2010.
It lies on the Gulf of Gonâve, on the island of Hispaniola.
Its National Palace collapsed in the 2010 quake.

Q883.name: Novosibirsk
facts: Founded in 1893 where the Trans-Siberian Railway crossed the Ob River.
Nearby Akademgorodok is a famous science town built in the Soviet era.
Its opera and ballet theatre is one of the largest theatre buildings in the world.

Q9365.name: Dushanbe
facts: Its name means 'Monday', after the weekly market held on the site.
It was called Stalinabad from 1929 to 1961.
It once held the world's tallest flagpole, 165 m high, raised in 2011.

Q49233.name: Orlando
facts: Walt Disney World and Universal theme parks are nearby, nicknaming it 'The City Beautiful'.
Kennedy Space Center at Cape Canaveral is about an hour to the east.
Home of the NBA's Magic, which joined the league in 1989.

Q9347.name: Malé
facts: A tiny coral island, it is one of the most densely populated cities on Earth.
Its international airport is on a separate island, linked by a bridge since 2018.
The Old Friday Mosque here is built from carved coral stone.

Q25282.name: Da Nang
facts: Its Dragon Bridge breathes fire and water on weekend nights.
The Golden Bridge, held up by giant stone hands, is in the nearby Ba Na Hills.
US Marines landed on its beaches in 1965; the Marble Mountains rise to the south.

Q11751.name: Nagoya
facts: Its castle is topped by golden shachihoko, tiger-headed fish ornaments.
Atsuta Shrine here is said to house the sacred sword Kusanagi, one of the imperial regalia.
It lies on Ise Bay, roughly midway between Tokyo and Osaka; Toyota is based nearby.

Q43196.name: Cincinnati
facts: Home of the Reds, descended from the first fully professional baseball team, of 1869.
Procter & Gamble was founded here in 1837.
Its Roebling Suspension Bridge across to Kentucky was a forerunner of the Brooklyn Bridge.

Q2096.name: Edmonton
facts: Home of North America's largest shopping mall, with an indoor waterpark and ice rink.
It sits on the North Saskatchewan River, and is often called the 'Gateway to the North'.
Its NHL team, the Oilers, won four Stanley Cups in the 1980s with Wayne Gretzky.

Q16666.name: Nanjing
facts: Its name means 'Southern Capital'; it was capital of several dynasties, including the early Ming.
The Mausoleum of Sun Yat-sen stands on Purple Mountain here.
It sits on the Yangtze, and its Ming-era city wall is one of the longest ever built.

Q3001.name: Paramaribo
facts: Its wooden colonial inner city is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
A large mosque and a synagogue stand side by side on the same street here.
Its St. Peter and Paul Cathedral is one of the largest wooden buildings in the Americas.

Q48278.name: Medellín
facts: Nicknamed the 'City of Eternal Spring' for its mild climate.
Artist Fernando Botero was born here, and its Flower Festival is famous.
Once linked to Pablo Escobar, it now uses cable cars to connect hillside neighbourhoods.

Q16565.name: Charlotte
facts: Its 'Queen City' nickname honours the wife of King George III.
A banking centre; Bank of America is headquartered here.
Home to the NASCAR Hall of Fame, the Hornets and the Panthers.

Q887.name: Yekaterinburg
facts: The Romanov royal family was executed here in 1918; the Church on the Blood marks the spot.
It lies on the eastern side of the Ural Mountains, near the Europe-Asia border.
Named after Catherine I, it was called Sverdlovsk in Soviet times.

Q8851.name: Málaga
facts: Pablo Picasso was born here in 1881.
Gateway to the Costa del Sol beaches, on the Mediterranean.
Antonio Banderas was born here; a Moorish fortress, the Alcazaba, overlooks the port.

Q2028.name: Verona
facts: Shakespeare set Romeo and Juliet here; 'Juliet's balcony' draws crowds.
Its Roman Arena still stages a summer opera festival.
It lies on the Adige river, near Lake Garda.

Q3646.name: Krasnodar
facts: Founded in 1793 as Yekaterinodar, 'Catherine's gift'.
It stands on the Kuban River, heartland of the Kuban Cossacks.
It is a gateway to the Black Sea resorts, a short drive to the south-west.

Q22889.name: Bath
facts: Its Roman baths are fed by the only natural hot springs on its island.
Jane Austen lived here and set parts of Persuasion and Northanger Abbey here.
Its Georgian Royal Crescent is a sweeping curve of 30 townhouses.

Q41819.name: Kansas City
facts: Famous for its barbecue, especially burnt ends.
Claims more fountains than any city except Rome, and is nicknamed the 'City of Fountains'.
Home of the NFL's Chiefs and the Negro Leagues Baseball Museum, at 18th and Vine.

Q11736.name: Tianjin
facts: A port city on the Bohai Sea, acting as the gateway to Beijing.
Famous for Goubuli steamed buns and a giant Ferris wheel built on a bridge over the Hai River.
It once had foreign concessions, leaving an Italian-style quarter in the city.

Q6610.name: Yakutsk
facts: Often called the coldest major city on Earth, with winter lows below -40.
Built on permafrost, many of its buildings stand on stilts.
It lies on the Lena River, in a region rich in diamonds and mammoth finds.

Q39121.name: Leeds
facts: Marks & Spencer began here as a market stall in 1884.
The earliest surviving film, Roundhay Garden Scene (1888), was shot here.
It lies on the River Aire, and is home to the Royal Armouries Museum.

Q43433.name: Chandigarh
facts: Planned in the 1950s by the architect Le Corbusier as a modernist city laid out in numbered sectors.
Home to Nek Chand's Rock Garden, built from recycled waste and broken ceramics.
Sits at the foothills of the Shivalik range and serves as the shared capital of two neighbouring states.

Q41183.name: Aleppo
facts: Its hilltop Citadel is one of the oldest and largest castles in the world.
Its covered souq, one of the world's largest historic markets, was badly damaged in the civil war from 2012.
Famous for laurel-oil soap and for being one of the oldest continuously inhabited cities on Earth.

Q3844.name: Brazzaville
facts: Sits on the Congo River directly opposite Kinshasa, another capital.
Named after the explorer Pierre Savorgnan de Brazza, who founded it in 1880.
It was the capital of Free France during the Second World War.

Q35178.name: Kuwait City
facts: Lies on a bay at the northwestern tip of the Persian Gulf.
Its skyline is marked by three slender water towers, two topped with blue-tiled spheres.
It was occupied by Iraqi forces in 1990, sparking the Gulf War.

Q78.name: Basel
facts: Sits on the Rhine where three countries meet, with France and Germany at its edges.
Hosts the world's leading modern art fair each June and is home to the Fondation Beyeler.
Roger Federer was born here, and it is home to pharmaceutical giants Novartis and Roche.

Q39420.name: Sochi
facts: A subtropical resort on the Black Sea coast with the Caucasus Mountains rising behind it.
Hosted the 2014 Winter Olympics, with the snow events held at nearby Krasnaya Polyana.
Stalin had a favourite summer dacha here, and it hosted Formula One races.

Q47492.name: Gaza City
facts: Lies on the Mediterranean coast in a narrow strip of land bordering Egypt and Israel.
In the Bible, Samson brought down the temple of the Philistines here.
One of the oldest cities in the world, it was a key stop on ancient incense trade routes.

Q3703.name: Bamako
facts: Sits on the Niger River, and its name is said to mean 'crocodile river'.
Famous for its music scene, home to stars such as Salif Keita and Amadou & Mariam.
Bridges such as the Martyrs' Bridge and King Fahd Bridge span the wide river through the city.

Q42941.name: Agra
facts: Home to the Taj Mahal, built by Shah Jahan as a tomb for his wife Mumtaz Mahal.
Sits on the Yamuna River and was the capital of the Mughal Empire.
Famous for petha, a sweet made from ash gourd, and for its Red Fort.

Q79980.name: Varanasi
facts: Hindus come to bathe and cremate their dead on the ghats lining the Ganges here.
One of the oldest continuously inhabited cities in the world, also known as Benares and Kashi.
Buddha gave his first sermon at nearby Sarnath, and it is famous for silk saris.

Q43421.name: Richmond
facts: Served as the capital of the Confederacy during the Civil War.
Patrick Henry gave his 'Give me liberty, or give me death!' speech in a church here.
Sits at the fall line of the James River, and Edgar Allan Poe grew up here.

Q38555.name: Santa Fe
facts: Founded around 1610, it is its country's oldest state capital and the highest, at about 7,000 feet.
Famous for its adobe buildings and the Palace of the Governors on its plaza.
Home to the Georgia O'Keeffe Museum and sits beneath the Sangre de Cristo Mountains.

Q41087.name: Raleigh
facts: Known as the 'City of Oaks' and a corner of the Research Triangle with Durham and Chapel Hill.
Named after the Elizabethan explorer who sponsored the lost Roanoke colony.
Home of the Hurricanes ice hockey team and part of the Research Triangle.

Q350.name: Cambridge
facts: Home to one of the world's oldest universities, founded in 1209.
Punting on the River Cam past the Backs and King's College Chapel is a classic pastime.
Watson and Crick announced the structure of DNA at the Eagle pub here in 1953.

Q13298.name: Graz
facts: Its old town is crowned by the Schlossberg hill and its clock tower, the Uhrturm.
Arnold Schwarzenegger grew up in a village just outside it.
The Mur River runs through it, crossed by the floating steel Murinsel island.

Q30002.name: Chengdu
facts: Home to a famous giant panda breeding research base.
Famous for spicy, numbing Sichuan pepper cuisine and hotpot.
Nearby Dujiangyan is an irrigation system over 2,000 years old that still works today.

Q39709.name: Des Moines
facts: Its state fair is famous for a life-size cow sculpted from butter.
Presidential hopefuls flock here every four years for the first-in-the-nation caucuses.
Sits where the Raccoon River meets a river sharing its name, and is a major insurance centre.

Q2135.name: Winnipeg
facts: Sits at the confluence of the Red and Assiniboine rivers, a meeting place called The Forks.
The bear that inspired Winnie-the-Pooh was named after this city.
Home to the national Museum for Human Rights and the Jets ice hockey team.

Q1722.name: Dubrovnik
facts: Its walled old town on the Adriatic was a filming location for King's Landing in Game of Thrones.
Historically called Ragusa, it was an independent maritime republic rivalling Venice.
Its complete ring of medieval walls can be walked all the way round.

Q41211.name: San Juan
facts: Its fortress El Morro has guarded the harbour since the 16th century.
Founded in 1521, it is one of the oldest European-founded cities in the Americas.
The pina colada is said to have been invented in a hotel here.

Q37400.name: Naypyidaw
facts: Built in secret and declared the capital in 2005, replacing Yangon.
Famous for enormous, near-empty highways with up to 20 lanes.
Home to the Uppatasanti Pagoda, a near-replica of the Shwedagon Pagoda.

Q2141.name: Halifax
facts: In 1917 a munitions ship exploded in its harbour, the largest man-made blast before the atomic bomb.
Over 100 victims of the Titanic are buried in its cemeteries.
A star-shaped Citadel overlooks one of the world's largest natural harbours on the Atlantic.

Q18383.name: Providence
facts: Founded in 1636 by Roger Williams as a haven for religious freedom.
Home to Brown University and a famous school of design, RISD.
Famous for WaterFire, when bonfires are lit on braziers in its downtown rivers.

Q40435.name: Buffalo
facts: Spicy chicken wings were invented at the Anchor Bar here in 1964.
Lies on Lake Erie at the head of the Niagara River, near Niagara Falls.
Famous for heavy lake-effect snow, chicken wings and its NFL team, the Bills.

Q2807.name: Madrid
facts: Home to the Prado Museum, with masterpieces by Velázquez and Goya.
Its football clubs include Real and Atlético, and it is famed for late-night dining.
Sits on the high central plateau, making it one of Europe's highest capitals.

Q1515.name: Abidjan
facts: Sits on the Ébrié Lagoon and was nicknamed the 'Paris of West Africa'.
Its modernist St Paul's Cathedral has a soaring tower meant to evoke the saint himself.
Its business district, Le Plateau, is famous for its skyscrapers; nearby is Grand-Bassam.

Q16520.name: Busan
facts: A major port at the southeastern tip of a peninsula, facing Japan across the Korea Strait.
Its Haeundae Beach is famous, and it hosts Asia's leading international film festival.
A famous zombie film follows a high-speed train heading here.

Q17042.name: Oakland
facts: The Black Panther Party was founded here in 1966.
Faces San Francisco across the bay, linked by the Bay Bridge.
Its Lake Merritt is a tidal lagoon in the middle of the city and the nation's oldest wildlife refuge.

Q35775.name: Boise
facts: Its university plays football on famous bright blue turf.
Its name is often said to come from French trappers crying 'les bois!' ('the woods!').
Sits in the Treasure Valley, where high desert meets mountain foothills.

Q24861.name: Albany
facts: Sits on the west bank of the Hudson River, near where the Mohawk joins it.
Founded by the Dutch as Fort Orange, it is one of the oldest surviving settlements of the original colonies.
