facts: The Minoan palace of Knossos lies just south of the city.
Novelist Nikos Kazantzakis, author of Zorba the Greek, is buried on its Venetian walls.
Its harbour is guarded by the Venetian Koules fortress; the painter El Greco was born in the area.

Q49273.name: Lubbock
facts: Rock 'n' roll pioneer Buddy Holly was born here in 1936.
Sits on the flat Llano Estacado and is nicknamed the Hub City.
A famous 1951 UFO sighting, a V of lights over the city, made national headlines.

Q22905.name: Bradford
facts: Grew rich as the wool capital of the world, nicknamed Worstedopolis.
Artist David Hockney was born here, and the Bronte sisters were born in nearby Thornton.
Famous for its curry houses, and home of the National Science and Media Museum.

Q126269.name: Wolverhampton
facts: Its football club, nicknamed Wolves, plays in old gold and black at Molineux.
Sunbeam cars and motorcycles were built here.
Lies on the edge of the Black Country, northwest of Birmingham.

Q79842.name: Flagstaff
facts: Pluto was discovered at its Lowell Observatory in 1930.
Became the world's first International Dark Sky City, protecting its night skies.
Sits on Route 66 beneath the San Francisco Peaks, a gateway to the Grand Canyon.

Q894.name: Samara
facts: Sits on a great bend of the Volga River.
Soyuz rockets that carry astronauts to space are built here.
As Kuybyshev, it was the wartime reserve capital, and Stalin's deep bunker survives here.

Q49179.name: Worcester
facts: The yellow smiley face was designed here in 1963 by Harvey Ball.
Rocket pioneer Robert Goddard was born here and launched the first liquid-fuel rocket nearby.
Famous for its classic diners, many built in prefab lunch-car factories in the city.

Q26590.name: Ciudad Juárez
facts: Sits across the Rio Grande from El Paso, linked by busy border bridges.
Was called Paso del Norte until 1888.
One of several places claimed as the birthplace of the margarita cocktail.

Q130514.name: Luxor
facts: Built on the site of ancient Thebes, beside the Nile.
Home to the vast temple complex of Karnak and an avenue of sphinxes linking it to a second great temple.
The Valley of the Kings, where Tutankhamun's tomb was found, lies across the river.

Q80517.name: Shreveport
facts: Sits on the Red River near where three states meet, a region called the Ark-La-Tex.
Elvis Presley rose to fame on a radio barn-dance show broadcast from here in the 1950s.
Known for riverboat casinos and nearby Barksdale Air Force Base.

Q50816.name: Mississauga
facts: Home to Toronto Pearson, the country's busiest airport.
In 1979, a train derailment forced over 200,000 residents to evacuate.
Its curvy Absolute World towers are nicknamed the Marilyn Monroe towers.

Q6397066.name: Shiraz
facts: The beloved poets Hafez and Saadi are buried here in garden tombs.
The ruins of Persepolis lie about 60 km to the northeast.
Famous for the Nasir al-Molk 'Pink Mosque', whose stained glass floods it with colour.

Q1513.name: Nagpur
facts: Called the Orange City for its famous oranges.
Ambedkar led a mass conversion to Buddhism here in 1956 at Deekshabhoomi.
Has a Zero Mile Stone, used in colonial surveys as the country's centre point.

Q49240.name: Stockton
facts: An inland seaport on the San Joaquin River delta, linked to San Francisco Bay.
Grew as a supply town for gold miners during the Gold Rush.
In 2012 it became the largest city in the country to have declared bankruptcy at the time.

Q3818.name: Malabo
facts: Lies on the north coast of Bioko island, once called Fernando Po.
Formerly named Santa Isabel under Spanish rule.
Overlooked by Pico Basile, a volcano that is the country's highest peak.

Q485186.name: Key West
facts: Ernest Hemingway's house here is famous for its many six-toed cats.
A striped buoy marks the southernmost point of the continental country, 90 miles from Cuba.
Crowds gather at Mallory Square every evening to cheer the sunset.

Q3940.name: Victoria
facts: One of the world's smallest capitals, on the northeast coast of Mahe island.
Its silver clock tower, Lorloz, is a copy of a clock in London.
A port in the Indian Ocean, originally called L'Etablissement by the French.

Q199605.name: Guwahati
facts: Sits on the banks of the mighty Brahmaputra River.
Home to the Kamakhya Temple, an important Hindu Shakti shrine on Nilachal Hill.
Its tea auction centre is one of the largest in the world.

Q43475.name: Derby
facts: Rolls-Royce has built aircraft engines here for over a century.
Lombe's Silk Mill here, from the 1720s, is often called the world's first modern factory.
Lies on the River Derwent; painter Joseph Wright was born here.

Q6576.name: Irkutsk
facts: Lies on the Angara River, about 70 km from Lake Baikal.
Exiled Decembrist rebels helped build its culture, earning it the name Paris of Siberia.
A major stop on the Trans-Siberian Railway.

Q29303.name: Canterbury
facts: Thomas Becket was murdered in its cathedral in 1170.
Chaucer's famous pilgrims were travelling here to Becket's shrine.
St Augustine arrived here in 597, and its archbishop is the senior bishop of the Anglican Communion.

Q171771.name: Bhubaneswar
facts: Known as the Temple City, home to the 11th-century Lingaraja Temple.
The Konark Sun Temple and the pilgrimage town of Puri lie nearby.
Hosted the men's Hockey World Cup in 2018 and 2023.

Q80484.name: Patna
facts: As Pataliputra, it was the capital of the Maurya Empire and Ashoka.
Stretches along the south bank of the Ganges.
Guru Gobind Singh, the tenth Sikh Guru, was born here.

Q170919.name: Pattaya
facts: Grew from a fishing village into a resort as a R&R spot for soldiers during the Vietnam War.
Its Sanctuary of Truth is a huge temple carved entirely from wood.
Famous for its neon Walking Street nightlife, about 150 km southeast of Bangkok.

Q134902.name: Stoke-on-Trent
facts: Known as The Potteries, home of Wedgwood, Spode and Royal Doulton.
Its skyline once bristled with thousands of bottle-shaped kilns.
Singer Robbie Williams was born here, and footballer Stanley Matthews too.

Q182852.name: Kunming
facts: Nicknamed the Spring City for its mild weather all year round.
The towering limestone pillars of the Stone Forest lie nearby.
Sits on the shore of Dian Lake; the Flying Tigers flew from here in World War II.

Q34739.name: Dayton
facts: Hometown of the Wright brothers, who built bicycles and their airplanes here.
Home of the national Air Force museum, the world's largest military aviation museum.
The cash register (NCR) and the pull-tab can opener were invented here.

Q66616.name: Indore
facts: Repeatedly ranked the cleanest city in the country.
Its Sarafa Bazaar becomes a famous night food market; poha and jalebi are breakfast staples.
Singer Lata Mangeshkar was born here; the Holkar dynasty's Rajwada palace stands in the centre.

Q171224.name: Eugene
facts: Nicknamed Track Town for its running heritage, home of the famous Hayward Field.
Coach Bill Bowerman co-founded Nike and made its first waffle-sole shoes here.
The film Animal House was shot at its university; it sits on the Willamette River.

Q3437.name: Perugia
facts: Home of Perugina and its Baci chocolates, and the Eurochocolate festival.
A hilltop city with an Etruscan arch, overlooking the Tiber valley.
Its University for Foreigners teaches the local language to students from around the world.

Q128114.name: Yonkers
facts: Elisha Otis founded his safety elevator company here in the 1850s.
Sits on the Hudson River, just north of the Bronx.
Singer Mary J. Blige and rapper DMX grew up here.

Q47465.name: Aix-en-Provence
facts: Painter Paul Cezanne was born here and painted nearby Mont Sainte-Victoire again and again.
Its grand avenue, the Cours Mirabeau, is lined with plane trees and fountains.
Founded by the Romans as Aquae Sextiae for its hot springs; famed for calisson sweets.

Q55630.name: Novi Sad
facts: Overlooked by the Petrovaradin Fortress on the Danube.
The fortress hosts EXIT, one of Europe's biggest music festivals.
Lies in the flat Pannonian plain and was European Capital of Culture in 2022.

Q81398.name: Acapulco de Juárez
facts: Cliff divers leap from the rocks of La Quebrada into the Pacific.
A Hollywood playground in the 1950s; JFK and Jackie honeymooned here.
Was the port for the Manila galleons trading with Asia; devastated by Hurricane Otis in 2023.

Q74881.name: Dalian
facts: Sits at the tip of the Liaodong Peninsula between the Bohai and Yellow seas.
Nearby Lushun was Port Arthur, besieged in the Russo-Japanese War.
Its Xinghai Square is one of the largest city squares in Asia.

Q1647.name: Rijeka
facts: The modern torpedo was developed here by Robert Whitehead in the 1860s.
Sits on the Kvarner Bay of the Adriatic, known historically as Fiume.
Hosts one of Europe's largest carnivals and was European Capital of Culture in 2020.

Q487119.name: Compton
facts: N.W.A's 1988 debut album, named after the city, put its gangsta rap scene on the map.
Venus and Serena Williams learned tennis on its public courts.
Rapper Kendrick Lamar and producer Dr. Dre grew up here, just south of downtown Los Angeles.

Q486306.name: Pensacola
facts: Home of the Blue Angels flight team, known as the Cradle of Naval Aviation.
Called the City of Five Flags for the many powers that ruled it.
Spain's 1559 settlement here was one of the first European colonies in the region; famed for white-sand beaches.

Q271395.name: Scranton
facts: The TV sitcom The Office is set at the Dunder Mifflin paper company here.
Nicknamed the Electric City for its early electric streetcars.
Joe Biden was born here in 1942.

Q13373.name: Lucca
facts: Encircled by intact Renaissance walls topped with a tree-lined promenade.
Composer Giacomo Puccini was born here.
Its oval Piazza dell'Anfiteatro follows a Roman amphitheatre, and the Guinigi Tower has trees on top.

Q79804.name: Sitka
facts: Once capital of Russian America; Russia handed the territory over here in 1867.
Overlooked by Mount Edgecumbe, a dormant volcano across the sound.
A national park here features Tlingit and Haida totem poles in a rainforest.

Q200713.name: Aurangabad
facts: Gateway to the rock-cut Ajanta and Ellora caves.
Its Bibi Ka Maqbara is nicknamed the Taj of the Deccan.
Named after the emperor Aurangzeb, who is buried nearby at Khuldabad.

Q49219.name: Irvine
facts: A master-planned city built on a huge former ranch in Orange County.
Video game company Blizzard Entertainment has its headquarters here.
Home to a university whose mascot is the Anteater.

Q3038.name: Heligoland
facts: A tiny red-sandstone island in the North Sea, famous for its rock stack, Lange Anna.
Britain swapped it for Zanzibar in 1890.
The words of today's national anthem were written here by Hoffmann von Fallersleben in 1841.

Q170263.name: Chester
facts: Encircled by the most complete Roman and medieval city walls in the land.
Famous for The Rows, two-level medieval shopping galleries.
Sits on the River Dee near the Welsh border; its Roodee is the oldest racecourse still in use.

Q93230.name: Rawalpindi
facts: Twin city of Islamabad and home of the army's General Headquarters.
Benazir Bhutto was assassinated in its Liaquat Bagh park in 2007.
Sits on the Pothohar Plateau; fast bowler Shoaib Akhtar was nicknamed after its express train.

Q3825.name: Libreville
facts: Its name means 'free town': it was settled by freed slaves in 1849.
Lies on the Komo River estuary, just north of the equator.
A port near the Gulf of Guinea, originally home of the Mpongwe people.

Q486472.name: Kansas City
facts: Sits across the state line from a bigger city of the same name in Missouri.
Lies where the Kaw River flows into the Missouri.
Has a NASCAR speedway and an MLS soccer stadium in its Village West district.

Q184775.name: Ipswich
facts: Sits at the head of the River Orwell estuary near the Suffolk coast.
Cardinal Thomas Wolsey, Henry VIII's chancellor, was born here.
Its football club, the Tractor Boys, won the league under Alf Ramsey and the UEFA Cup under Bobby Robson.

Q2742.name: Münster
facts: The 1648 peace treaty ending the Thirty Years' War was signed here.
Famous as a bicycle city, with more bikes than people.
Three iron cages hang from St. Lambert's church tower, where Anabaptist leaders' bodies were displayed.

Q3104.name: Koblenz
facts: Its Deutsches Eck headland marks where the Moselle flows into the Rhine.
The Romans named it Confluentes, meaning 'confluence'.
A cable car crosses the Rhine to the huge Ehrenbreitstein Fortress.

Q46747.name: Sendai
facts: Founded by the one-eyed samurai lord Date Masamune, whose statue overlooks it.
Its Tanabata festival fills the streets with giant paper streamers each August.
Known as the City of Trees and for grilled beef tongue; hit by the 2011 Tohoku tsunami.

Q51689.name: Plano
facts: Frito-Lay, Pizza Hut and Toyota's regional arm all have their headquarters here.
Its name is Spanish for 'flat', after the level prairie it was built on.
A big suburb just north of Dallas, it holds a hot-air balloon festival every year.

Q66568.name: Kanpur
facts: Under British rule it was known as Cawnpore.
The city sits on the south bank of the Ganges.
It was the scene of a famous siege and massacre during the 1857 rebellion against British rule.

Q574192.name: Greenville
facts: A curved suspension bridge in Falls Park looks over waterfalls on the Reedy River downtown.
It lies on I-85, roughly halfway between Atlanta and Charlotte, in the Blue Ridge foothills.
Baseball legend 'Shoeless' Joe Jackson grew up here, and his house is now a museum.

Q1724.name: Saarbrücken
facts: It sits on the Saar river, right on the border with France's Moselle department.
Its baroque Ludwigskirche is one of the best-known Protestant baroque churches in its country.
It hosts the Max Ophüls Prize, a well-known festival for young filmmakers.

Q134672.name: Exeter
facts: It sits on the River Exe, near where the river widens into an estuary on the Channel coast.
Its Gothic cathedral has the longest unbroken medieval stone vaulted ceiling in the world.
Medieval tunnels that once carried fresh water run under its streets, and you can tour them.

Q131633.name: Hallstatt
facts: This tiny lakeside village sits between the Hallstätter See and the steep Dachstein mountains.
Its salt mine is often called the oldest in the world, worked for about 7,000 years.
A full-size copy of the village was built in Guangdong, China, in 2012.

Q49268.name: Fort Wayne
facts: The St. Joseph and St. Marys rivers meet here to form the Maumee River.
Johnny Appleseed, the folk hero who planted apple trees, is buried here.
It is named after the Revolutionary War general 'Mad' Anthony Wayne.

Q51691.name: Amarillo
facts: Cadillac Ranch, a row of ten graffiti-covered Cadillacs half-buried nose-down, is just west of town.
Its name is Spanish for 'yellow', and it is the largest city on the panhandle's high plains.
Old Route 66 runs through town, and a steakhouse here gives you a 72-ounce steak free if you finish it in an hour.

Q81788.name: Giza
facts: The Great Pyramid and the Great Sphinx stand on its desert edge.
It lies on the west bank of the Nile, across from central Cairo.
A huge new museum built next to the pyramids holds Tutankhamun's treasures.

Q3904.name: Mbabane
facts: It shares capital duties with nearby Lobamba, the royal and legislative capital.
It is high in the Mdzimba Mountains of a small landlocked kingdom between South Africa and Mozambique.
Sibebe Rock nearby is one of the largest exposed granite domes in the world.

Q3370.name: Zadar
facts: Its Sea Organ plays music as Adriatic waves push air through pipes under marble steps.
Alfred Hitchcock is said to have called its sunset the most beautiful in the world.
Under its Venetian name, Zara, it became famous for maraschino cherry liqueur.

Q5760.name: Thebes
facts: In myth it was the city of Oedipus, who killed his father and married his mother.
Its elite Sacred Band was made up of 150 pairs of male lovers.
Alexander the Great razed the city in 335 BC, sparing only the house of the poet Pindar.

Q11462.name: Surabaya
facts: Its symbol is a shark fighting a crocodile, which is said to be where the name comes from.
A fierce battle here in November 1945 is remembered every year as the nation's Heroes' Day.
The Suramadu Bridge crosses the Madura Strait from here to Madura island.

Q1851.name: Arkhangelsk
facts: It sits where the Northern Dvina River flows into the White Sea.
Allied Arctic convoys brought war supplies here in World War II.
It was named after the Archangel Michael monastery, and in English it was long just called 'Archangel'.

Q49221.name: Scottsdale
facts: Frank Lloyd Wright built Taliesin West, his winter home and school, in the desert here.
Fans pack a golf tournament here with a famously rowdy 16th hole, ringed by stands.
This Phoenix suburb sits by the McDowell Mountains in the Sonoran Desert.

Q48370.name: Manchester
facts: Its Amoskeag Mills on the Merrimack River were once the largest cotton textile mills in the world.
Comedian Adam Sandler grew up here.
Presidential hopefuls crowd in here every four years before the first-in-the-nation primary.

Q3012.name: Ulm
facts: Its minster has the tallest church steeple in the world, about 161 m high.
Albert Einstein was born here in 1879.
It sits on the Danube, and in 1811 a tailor tried to glide across the river and fell into it.

Q6506.name: Varna
facts: Gold found in a cemetery here, more than 6,000 years old, is the oldest worked gold in the world.
In Bram Stoker's novel, Dracula sails from this Black Sea port to Whitby.
A crusader army lost to the Ottomans here in 1444.

Q1473.name: Davao City
facts: Mount Apo, the country's highest peak, rises just west of the city.
It is a big city on Mindanao, and the spiky, smelly durian fruit is its symbol.
Rodrigo Duterte was its mayor for over 20 years before becoming president.

Q192517.name: Boulder
facts: The Flatirons, huge slanted rock slabs, rise over the city at the foot of the Rockies.
The 1970s sitcom Mork & Mindy was set here.
Its Memorial Day 10K road race is one of the biggest in the world, with tens of thousands of runners.

Q41843.name: Beersheba
facts: Genesis says Abraham dug a well here and swore an oath, which gives it its name.
Australian Light Horsemen made a famous cavalry charge to take it in 1917.
It is the biggest city in the Negev desert.

Q40816.name: Benghazi
facts: It is a Mediterranean port on the Gulf of Sidra, first founded as the Greek colony Euesperides.
The 2011 uprising against Muammar Gaddafi started here.
A 2012 attack on the US mission here killed Ambassador Chris Stevens.

Q42807.name: Nîmes
facts: Its Maison Carrée is one of the best-preserved Roman temples anywhere.
The word denim comes from serge fabric made here ('serge de ...').
The Pont du Gard, a famous Roman aqueduct bridge, once carried water to the city.

Q3932.name: São Tomé
facts: This port is on an island in the Gulf of Guinea, just north of the Equator.
Its island once grew more cocoa than anywhere else in the world.
The Pico Cão Grande, a strange needle of volcanic rock, rises from the jungle on the same island.

Q170377.name: Blackpool
facts: Its tower, opened in 1894, was modeled on the Eiffel Tower.
Every autumn its Illuminations light up about 10 km of Irish Sea seafront.
Its Pleasure Beach is home to the Big One roller coaster, and its trams are among the world's oldest electric ones.

Q644.name: Sharm el-Sheikh
facts: It is a Red Sea resort at the southern tip of the Sinai Peninsula, famous for scuba diving.
Ras Mohammed National Park, with its coral reefs, is just to the south.
It hosted the COP27 UN climate summit in 2022.

Q93347.name: Mostar
facts: Its Stari Most, an arched Ottoman bridge from 1566, was destroyed in 1993 and rebuilt in 2004.
Divers jump more than 20 m from the old bridge into the Neretva River.
Its name comes from the bridge keepers who guarded the crossing in Ottoman times.

Q44210.name: Córdoba
facts: Its Jesuit Block, with one of the oldest universities in the Americas, is a UNESCO site.
It sits at the foot of the Sierras Chicas, and its learned past earned it the nickname 'La Docta'.
Fernet and Coke is the local drink, and the city gave its name to cuarteto, a lively dance music.

Q29422.name: Boca Raton
facts: IBM built its first personal computer, the IBM PC, at a lab here in 1981.
Its name comes from Spanish words often translated as 'mouth of the rat'.
Architect Addison Mizner built its pink Mediterranean-style resort in the 1920s, on the Atlantic coast.

Q3739.name: Bissau
facts: It sits on the estuary of the Geba River, where it meets the Atlantic.
The Bijagós Islands, with saltwater hippos, lie offshore.
The Pidjiguiti dock massacre here in 1959 sparked Amílcar Cabral's fight for independence.

Q1140136.name: Ciudad de la Paz
facts: This brand-new capital is being built from scratch in the rainforest of the mainland.
It was planned partly because an inland capital was seen as safer after a 2004 coup attempt.
It was once called Oyala, and its name means 'City of Peace'.

Q9885.name: Coimbatore
facts: It is nicknamed the 'Manchester of the South' for its many cotton mills.
It sits on the Noyyal River by the Western Ghats, near the Palakkad Gap.
A 34 m bust of Shiva, the Adiyogi, stands at an ashram on its outskirts.

Q6548.name: Orléans
facts: Joan of Arc broke the English siege of the city in 1429, earning her famous nickname.
It sits on the Loire, at the northernmost point of the river's great bend.
Its Gothic Sainte-Croix Cathedral was rebuilt by the Bourbon kings after the Wars of Religion.

Q320792.name: Bata
facts: It is the biggest city of a country whose capital was long on Bioko island, across the sea.
This Atlantic port on the Río Muni mainland has ferries to Malabo and Douala.
It is known for its seafront promenade, its nightlife and its big market.

Q485716.name: Glendale
facts: Walt Disney, Michael Jackson and Humphrey Bogart are buried in its Forest Lawn cemetery.
It is home to one of the largest Armenian communities outside Armenia.
It sits by the Verdugo Mountains, about 10 miles north of downtown Los Angeles.

Q11909.name: Vadodara
facts: Its Laxmi Vilas Palace is said to be four times the size of Buckingham Palace.
It was long ruled by the Gaekwad maharajas, and was known as Baroda.
It is named after its many banyan trees, and crocodiles live in the river through town.

Q25475.name: Batumi
facts: This Black Sea resort is about 20 km north of the border with Turkey.
Its moving steel sculpture 'Ali and Nino' shows two lovers who slowly pass through each other.
Its subtropical botanical garden sits on cliffs above the sea, and casinos line its waterfront.

Q83786.name: Shimla
facts: It was the summer capital of the British Raj, high in the Himalayan foothills.
The narrow-gauge Kalka railway that climbs here is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
A 33 m statue of Hanuman stands on Jakhu Hill, the highest point in town.

Q88.name: Alexandria
facts: It sits on the Potomac River, just across from Washington, D.C.
George Washington's home, Mount Vernon, is just to the south.
The football film Remember the Titans tells a true story from one of its high schools.

Q49174.name: Bridgeport
facts: Showman P.T. Barnum was once its mayor, and General Tom Thumb was born here.
The first Subway sandwich shop opened here in 1965.
It is a port on Long Island Sound, about 60 miles from Manhattan.

Q26426.name: Montpelier
facts: It is the smallest state capital by population in the whole nation.
It is the only state capital without a McDonald's.
Its State House has a gold dome and sits on the Winooski River.

Q289693.name: Sharjah
facts: UNESCO named it the Cultural Capital of the Arab World in 1998.
It is right next to Dubai, and the two have grown into one big city.
It has the strictest rules in its federation, banning alcohol completely.

Q49158.name: Springfield
facts: James Naismith invented basketball here in 1891, and the sport's Hall of Fame is here.
Dr. Seuss (Theodor Geisel) was born and grew up here.
It sits on the Connecticut River, and Smith & Wesson guns are made here.

Q38545.name: Adana
facts: A spicy minced-meat kebab cooked on a skewer is named after the city.
The Roman stone bridge Taşköprü still crosses the Seyhan River here.
It sits on the fertile Çukurova plain near the Mediterranean, and İncirlik Air Base is nearby.

Q182625.name: Windsor
facts: It is right across the Detroit River from Detroit, and oddly, it lies south of that city.
The Ambassador Bridge and a tunnel under the river connect it to Detroit.
Hiram Walker's big whisky distillery is here, and it was a hub for Prohibition rum-running.

Q186040.name: Ayodhya
facts: Hindus believe the god Rama was born here.
A huge new Ram Mandir temple opened here in 2024, where the Babri Masjid stood until 1992.
It sits on the banks of the Sarayu River, and its Deepotsav festival lights millions of oil lamps.

Q2683.name: Parma
facts: Both a famous hard cheese and a cured ham are named after it.
Conductor Arturo Toscanini was born here, and Verdi was born nearby.
Barilla, the world's biggest pasta maker, has its home here.

Q83404.name: Timișoara
facts: In 1884 it became one of the first cities in Europe with electric street lights.
The 1989 revolution that brought down Ceaușescu started here.
It sits on the Bega River in the Banat region and was a European Capital of Culture in 2023.

Q238508.name: Gurgaon
facts: Its official name was changed to honor Guru Dronacharya, the teacher in the Mahabharata.
This glass-tower office city next to Delhi is home to many global companies and call centers.
It is right next to Delhi's Indira Gandhi International Airport.

Q499681.name: Coeur d'Alene
facts: It sits on the north shore of a big mountain lake of the same name.
A resort here has a famous floating golf green that you reach by boat.
Fur traders gave a local tribe its French name, meaning 'heart of an awl'.

Q48195.name: Basra
facts: Sinbad the Sailor began his voyages from this port, according to legend.
It sits on the Shatt al-Arab, where the Tigris and Euphrates join, close to the Iran border.
Its canals once made people call it the 'Venice of the East', and date palms grow all around.

Q36399.name: Huế
facts: It was the imperial capital of the Nguyễn emperors, and its walled Citadel is a UNESCO site.
The Perfume River flows through the city.
It was the scene of one of the bloodiest battles of the 1968 Tet Offensive.

Q131128.name: Braunau am Inn
facts: Adolf Hitler was born here in 1889.
It is a border town on the Inn River, across from Simbach in Bavaria.
Bookseller Johann Philipp Palm was shot here in 1806 on Napoleon's orders.

Q49238.name: Greensboro
facts: The 1960 Woolworth's lunch counter sit-in, a key moment of the civil rights movement, started here.
Vicks VapoRub was invented here, and Wrangler jeans were started here.
Writer O. Henry was born here.

Q157835.name: Zaporizhzhia
facts: The Cossacks' fortress was on Khortytsia, a large island in the Dnieper here.
The huge DniproHES hydroelectric dam crosses the Dnieper here.
A cheap little Soviet car, nicknamed the 'humpback', was built here.

Q83387.name: Diyarbakır
facts: Its massive black basalt walls are among the longest city walls in the world.
It sits above the Tigris, which the old Ten-Eyed Bridge crosses below the city.
It is famous for giant watermelons, celebrated at a yearly festival.

Q6454.name: Calais
facts: It is the closest port to Dover, just across the Strait of Dover.
Rodin's famous sculpture of six burghers marks how its citizens offered their lives in 1347.
England held it until 1558, and Mary I supposedly said its name would be found written on her heart.

Q1729.name: Erfurt
facts: Martin Luther studied here and became a monk at its Augustinian monastery.
Its Krämerbrücke is a medieval bridge lined with lived-in houses, over the Gera river.
Its Old Synagogue is one of the oldest synagogues still standing in Europe.

Q51103.name: Cali
facts: It calls itself the world capital of salsa dancing.
A notorious drug cartel of the 1980s and 1990s was named after it.
A Christ statue looks down on the city from the hills above the Cauca River valley.

Q7024.name: Lugano
facts: It sits on a lake between Monte San Salvatore and Monte Brè, near the border with Italy.
The first Eurovision Song Contest was held here in 1956.
It is the largest Italian-speaking city in its country, and a big banking center.

Q3792.name: Lomé
facts: This coastal capital sits right on the border with Ghana, on the Gulf of Guinea.
Its Akodessewa market is one of the world's largest markets for voodoo charms.
Its market women, the 'Nana Benz', got rich trading wax-print cloth and drove Mercedes cars.

Q133073.name: Dunedin
facts: Its name is the Scottish Gaelic name for Edinburgh, and it was founded by Scottish settlers.
Guinness has ranked its Baldwin Street as the steepest residential street in the world.
The only mainland breeding colony of royal albatross is on the peninsula nearby.

Q202973.name: Kingston
facts: Fort Henry overlooks the place where Lake Ontario becomes the St. Lawrence River.
It is at the south end of the Rideau Canal and next to the Thousand Islands.
The first prime minister, Sir John A. Macdonald, grew up here, and it was briefly the capital in the 1840s.

Q4629.name: Surat
facts: Most of the world's diamonds are cut and polished here.
The English East India Company opened one of its first trading posts here in the early 1600s.
It sits on the Tapti River near the Arabian Sea and is a big center for textiles and silk.

Q648501.name: Asheville
facts: The Biltmore Estate here is the largest privately owned house in the nation.
It sits in the Blue Ridge Mountains where the French Broad and Swannanoa rivers meet.
Novelist Thomas Wolfe grew up here and wrote about it in Look Homeward, Angel.

Q40898.name: Nancy
facts: Its 18th-century Place Stanislas, with gilded gates, is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
It was a center of Art Nouveau, known for glassmakers like Émile Gallé and Daum.
Charles the Bold, Duke of Burgundy, was killed in a battle here in 1477.

Q199528.name: Dehradun
facts: It lies in the Doon Valley at the foot of the Himalayas, below Mussoorie.
The country's top military academy and the famous Doon School are here.
Its grand Forest Research Institute building is one of the largest brick buildings in Asia.

Q486168.name: San Bernardino
facts: The McDonald brothers opened the first McDonald's here in 1940.
A huge arrowhead-shaped bare patch on the mountainside above the city is a famous landmark.
Old Route 66 passes through town at the foot of the Cajon Pass.

Q49227.name: Winston-Salem
facts: R.J. Reynolds made Camel cigarettes here.
Krispy Kreme doughnuts started here in 1937.
It was formed by joining two towns, one of them an 18th-century Moravian settlement that you can still visit.

Q142811.name: Allentown
facts: The Liberty Bell was hidden under a church floor here during the Revolutionary War.
Billy Joel's 1982 song about a fading steel town is named after it.
It sits on the Lehigh River, and Mack Trucks have long been built in the area.

Q125434.name: Gqeberha
facts: It was long called Port Elizabeth, and it lies on Algoa Bay.
Its city council is named Nelson Mandela Bay, and it is known as the 'Windy City'.
Addo Elephant National Park is just north of the city.

Q40104.name: Ajaccio
facts: Napoleon Bonaparte was born here in 1769.
It sits on a gulf on the west coast of a mountainous Mediterranean island.
The red Îles Sanguinaires sit at the mouth of its gulf, and singer Tino Rossi was born here.

Q50189.name: Annecy
facts: It sits at the north end of a clear Alpine lake, about 35 km south of Geneva.
Its canals give it the nickname 'Venice of the Alps', and the Palais de l'Isle is on an island in a canal.
It hosts the world's top animation film festival every June.

Q174091.name: Changsha
facts: A giant sculpture of a young Mao Zedong's head stands on Orange Isle in the Xiang River here.
The Mawangdui tombs here held the 2,000-year-old Lady Dai, one of the best-preserved bodies ever found.
It is famous for its stinky tofu and for the old Yuelu Academy.

Q906.name: Chelyabinsk
facts: A meteor exploded over the city in 2013, blowing out windows and injuring over 1,000 people.
Its tank factories in World War II gave it the nickname 'Tankograd'.
It lies just east of the Ural Mountains, at the gateway to Siberia.

Q10086.name: Mysore
facts: Its palace is lit up with nearly 100,000 light bulbs on Sundays and holidays.
Its 10-day Dasara festival, with a parade of elephants, is famous across the country.
It is known for silk, sandalwood and a rich ghee sweet named after the city.

Q49229.name: Durham
facts: Duke University and its Blue Devils are here, along with the gothic Duke Chapel.
The 1988 baseball film with Kevin Costner was named after its minor-league team.
It is one corner of the Research Triangle, and was once a tobacco town.

Q57278.name: Newcastle
facts: It sits at the mouth of the Hunter River and is the world's biggest coal-export port.
The Hunter Valley wine country lies just inland.
Convicts cut the Bogey Hole, a rock pool, into the cliffs here.

Q157725.name: Chernivtsi
facts: Its university building, the old palace of the Orthodox bishops, is a UNESCO site.
It sits on the Prut River and was once the capital of Bukovina, near the border with Romania.
The poet Paul Celan was born here when it was part of Austria-Hungary.

Q47837.name: Laayoune
facts: It is the largest city in Western Sahara, a territory whose control is disputed.
It was founded by a Spanish army captain in 1938 and became the capital of the Spanish Sahara.
Phosphate rock is carried to the coast near here on a conveyor belt about 100 km long.

Q38380.name: Angers
facts: Its castle holds the Apocalypse Tapestry, the largest medieval tapestry still in existence.
Cointreau, the orange liqueur, was created here.
It was the main city of Anjou, the home of the Plantagenet kings, near the Loire.

Q41963.name: Sri Jayawardenepura Kotte
facts: Parliament meets in a building on an island in a lake here.
It is right next to Colombo, the main commercial city.
It was a royal capital in the 15th century, when the island had several kingdoms.

Q20927.name: Daegu
facts: Samsung began here in 1938 as a small trading company.
It sits in a bowl of mountains and is famous for being hot in summer and for its apples.
Its herbal medicine market, Yangnyeongsi, has been running since the 1600s.

Q189602.name: Missoula
facts: Norman Maclean's A River Runs Through It is set in and near this town.
It sits on the Clark Fork River, where five mountain ranges meet.
Smokejumpers, the firefighters who parachute in, have their largest training base here.

Q185632.name: Limassol
facts: Richard the Lionheart married Berengaria of Navarre here in 1191.
The Crusader castle of Kolossi nearby is where the sweet wine Commandaria was made.
It is a port on the island's south coast, between the old towns of Amathus and Kourion.

Q147402.name: Zapopan
facts: A small, very old statue of the Virgin from its basilica is carried to Guadalajara each year.
Estadio Akron, home of the Chivas football club, is here and hosted 2026 World Cup matches.
It is part of Guadalajara's metro area, just to the northwest.

Q133529.name: Vorkuta
facts: It was built around Gulag prison camps, where prisoners mined coal.
It lies north of the Arctic Circle, and it is the easternmost town in Europe.
It has the coldest temperature recorded in any European city, -52 C.

Q185458.name: Quetta
facts: It is in a valley surrounded by mountains, near the Bolan Pass and the Afghan border.
A 1935 earthquake almost completely destroyed the city.
Its orchards are famous for apples, grapes and dried fruit.

Q2765.name: Gelsenkirchen
facts: Schalke 04 plays here, in an arena whose grass pitch slides out of the stadium.
Its coal mines once made it a top coal-mining city, called the 'city of a thousand fires'.
It sits on the Emscher River and hosted games at the 2006 World Cup and Euro 2024.

Q151993.name: Ruhr Region
facts: It includes Essen, Dortmund, Duisburg and Bochum, all grown together into one big urban area.
It was the heart of coal and steel, and Zollverein in Essen is now a UNESCO site.
Duisburg, where it meets the Rhine, has one of the largest inland ports in the world.

Q58976.name: Piraeus
facts: It is the port of Athens, from where ferries leave for the islands.
In ancient times, the Long Walls linked it to Athens.
Olympiacos football club plays here, and the film Never on Sunday was set here.

Q192240.name: Northampton
facts: It is famous for making shoes, and the musical Kinky Boots is set in one of its factories.
It sits on the River Nene, and its rugby team is called the Saints.
Comic-book writer Alan Moore lives here and has written about the town.

Q181962.name: Augusta
facts: The Masters golf tournament is played here every April.
James Brown, the 'Godfather of Soul', grew up here.
It sits on the Savannah River, on the border with South Carolina, at the head of navigation.

Q155975.name: Kutná Hora
facts: The Sedlec Ossuary here has a chandelier made from human bones.
Its silver mines were very rich, and the Prague groschen coin was minted here.
St. Barbara's, a great Gothic church, was named after the saint of miners.

Q2973.name: Darmstadt
facts: Element 110 was discovered and named here.
The European Space Agency runs its satellite control center (ESOC) here.
Merck, the world's oldest pharmaceutical company, is based here, and Frankenstein Castle is nearby.

Q37333.name: Lublin
facts: A union signed here in 1569 joined the kingdom with Lithuania in one commonwealth.
The Nazi death camp Majdanek was on its outskirts.
The chapel in its castle is decorated with Byzantine-style frescoes.

Q487315.name: Monterey
facts: Steinbeck's novel Cannery Row is named after its street of sardine canneries.
Its big aquarium is in an old cannery on the bay.
Jimi Hendrix set his guitar on fire at a famous 1967 pop festival here.

Q487999.name: Gainesville
facts: Gatorade was invented here in 1965 for the local university's football team, the Gators.
Rock singer Tom Petty was born and grew up here.
Wild bison and horses roam the Paynes Prairie savanna on the south edge of town.

Q172343.name: Rafah
facts: Its border crossing into Egypt is the only way out of the Gaza Strip that avoids Israel.
Ptolemy IV beat Antiochus III in a huge battle with war elephants here in 217 BC.
It was split by a border in 1982, with part of the town left on the Sinai side.

Q217346.name: Ithaca
facts: It sits at the south end of Cayuga Lake, one of the Finger Lakes.
Cornell University sits on a hill above the town.
The town's slogan is a pun on 'gorgeous', thanks to all its waterfalls and gorges.

Q131818.name: Oran
facts: Albert Camus set his novel The Plague in this Mediterranean port.
Considered the birthplace of rai music, made famous by singers like Cheb Khaled.
Fashion designer Yves Saint Laurent was born here in 1936.

Q569678.name: Bozeman
facts: Its Museum of the Rockies holds one of the largest collections of dinosaur fossils anywhere.
Sits in the Gallatin Valley, about 90 miles north of Yellowstone National Park.
Named after a pioneer who blazed a wagon trail to the gold fields in the 1860s.

Q659400.name: Wilmington
facts: A World War II battleship is moored here as a museum on the Cape Fear River.
Michael Jordan grew up here and played high school basketball in the city.
Nicknamed 'Hollywood East', it was the filming base for Dawson's Creek and One Tree Hill.

Q68744.name: Xiamen
facts: Known to Western traders as Amoy, it faces the Taiwan Strait and the island of Kinmen.
Its car-free Gulangyu islet, nicknamed 'Piano Island', is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
The English word 'tea' is thought to come from 'te' in the local Hokkien dialect.

Q83236.name: Chamonix-Mont-Blanc
facts: Hosted the very first Winter Olympic Games in 1924.
Sits at the foot of the highest mountain in the Alps, reached by the Aiguille du Midi cable car.
The Mer de Glace, a famous glacier, flows down from the peaks above town.

Q128244.name: Waco
facts: Dr Pepper was invented at a drugstore here in 1885.
Site of the 1993 siege of the Branch Davidian compound.
Home to Baylor University and Magnolia Market from TV's Fixer Upper, on the Brazos River.

Q135744.name: Galveston
facts: The 1900 hurricane that struck here remains the deadliest natural disaster in its country's history.
Juneteenth began here, when news of emancipation was announced on 19 June 1865.
A barrier island city on the Gulf of Mexico, southeast of Houston.

Q45313.name: Herat
facts: Its ancient citadel is said to date back to Alexander the Great.
Once the glittering Timurid capital, famous for its Friday Mosque and leaning Musalla minarets.
Lies in the Hari River valley near the Iranian border, on old Silk Road routes.

Q3927.name: Astrakhan
facts: Sits on the Volga delta near the Caspian Sea, famous for sturgeon and caviar.
Its white-walled 16th-century kremlin overlooks the river.
Also renowned for its huge, sweet watermelons.

Q49169.name: Stamford
facts: Sits on Long Island Sound, a short train ride from New York City.
Home to the headquarters of WWE, the professional wrestling company.
Nicknamed 'The Lock City' for the Yale & Towne lock factory that once dominated it.

Q3876.name: Lilongwe
facts: Became the capital in 1975, replacing the old colonial capital of Zomba.
Founding president Hastings Kamuzu Banda lies in a grand mausoleum here.
Its auction floors sell tobacco, the nation's leading export crop.

Q2773.name: Brunswick
facts: The mathematician Carl Friedrich Gauss was born here in 1777.
A bronze lion statue honours Henry the Lion, the medieval duke who made it his seat.
Lies on the Oker river, between Hanover and Wolfsburg.

Q156732.name: Kherson
facts: A port on the Dnieper River, just upstream from where it meets the Black Sea.
Founded in 1778 by Prince Grigory Potemkin, who is buried in its cathedral.
Its region is famous for growing watermelons and tomatoes.

Q164380.name: Bethlehem
facts: Founded by Moravian settlers on Christmas Eve 1741, it calls itself 'Christmas City'.
Its giant steelworks made steel for the Golden Gate Bridge and many skyscrapers.
Sits on the Lehigh River and is home to Lehigh University.

Q170521.name: Kashgar
facts: A Silk Road oasis on the western edge of the Taklamakan Desert.
Famous for its Id Kah Mosque and huge Sunday livestock bazaar.
The Karakoram Highway runs from here over the mountains to Pakistan.

Q189133.name: Cairns
facts: The main gateway to the Great Barrier Reef.
The Daintree Rainforest lies just to the north.
The Kuranda Scenic Railway and Skyrail cableway climb from here into the rainforest.

Q179815.name: Durham
facts: Its Norman cathedral and castle stand on a rocky peninsula in a loop of the River Wear.
The cathedral cloisters appeared as Hogwarts in the first Harry Potter film.
The Venerable Bede and St Cuthbert are buried in its cathedral.

Q7568.name: Yogyakarta
facts: The great Buddhist temple of Borobudur lies nearby, as do the Hindu temples of Prambanan.
Still ruled by a sultan, whose Kraton palace stands in the city centre.
The active volcano Mount Merapi looms to the north.

Q28180.name: Jefferson City
facts: Named after a president who sent Lewis and Clark up the river it sits on.
Its domed capitol stands on a bluff above the river.
Boxer Sonny Liston and James Earl Ray were once held in its old penitentiary.

Q46852.name: Iași
facts: Home to the country's oldest university, founded in 1860.
The national poet Mihai Eminescu lived and wrote here.
Its grand neo-Gothic Palace of Culture is a landmark near the Prut river border.

Q233129.name: Peoria
facts: Vaudeville gave rise to the phrase 'Will it play here?', a test of mainstream appeal.
Mass production of penicillin was pioneered at a lab here, using mould from a cantaloupe.
Comedian Richard Pryor was born here; it was long home to Caterpillar.

Q2861.name: Rostock
facts: A Baltic Sea port whose beach resort of Warnemünde lines the coast.
A medieval Hanseatic League city with a university founded in 1419.
Hosts Hanse Sail, a huge annual gathering of tall ships.

Q187136.name: Luoyang
facts: The Longmen Grottoes hold tens of thousands of Buddha statues carved into cliffs here.
The White Horse Temple here is said to be the first Buddhist temple in the land.
An ancient capital beside the Yellow River, famous for its spring peony festival.

Q173148.name: Delos
facts: In Greek myth, Apollo and Artemis were born on this island.
Its ancient Terrace of the Lions is a famous sight, a short boat ride from Mykonos.
Once the treasury of the Delian League, it is now almost uninhabited.

Q13498.name: Taranto
facts: The tarantula spider and the tarantella dance are named after this city.
Founded by Spartans as Taras, it sits on the instep of the boot's heel.
Lies on two seas, the Mar Grande and the Mar Piccolo, and is a major naval base.

Q915.name: Perm
facts: A geological period, ending with the greatest mass extinction, is named after this area.
Sits on the Kama River at the foot of the Ural Mountains.
Was called Molotov from 1940 to 1957; a preserved gulag camp lies nearby.

Q135615.name: Springfield
facts: Calls itself the birthplace of Route 66, whose name was proposed here in 1926.
Home to the flagship store and headquarters of Bass Pro Shops.
Wild Bill Hickok shot Davis Tutt on its town square in 1865, in the Ozarks.

Q80561.name: Antakya
facts: Ancient Antioch, where followers of Jesus were first called Christians.
Its cave Church of St Peter is one of the oldest Christian sites.
Lies on the Orontes River and was devastated by the 2023 earthquakes.

Q154814.name: Bandar Abbas
facts: A port on the Strait of Hormuz, the gateway to the Gulf's oil routes.
Named after Shah Abbas I, who seized it from the Portuguese in 1622.
Faces the islands of Qeshm and Hormuz across the water.

Q12919.name: Majuro
facts: A thin ring of coral islets around a lagoon, linked by one long road.
Barely a few metres above sea level, it is threatened by rising seas.
The region's navigators once used stick charts made of palm ribs and shells.

Q203889.name: Luton
facts: Once the hat-making capital, its football club is still nicknamed 'the Hatters'.
Lies at the source of the River Lea, north of London.
Its stadium, Kenilworth Road, is famous for an entrance through a row of houses.

Q2865.name: Kassel
facts: Hosts documenta, a major contemporary art exhibition held every five years.
The Brothers Grimm lived and collected their fairy tales here.
Its Bergpark Wilhelmshöhe, crowned by a giant Hercules statue, is a World Heritage Site.

Q54264.name: Newport
facts: Famed for Gilded Age mansions like The Breakers, built by the Vanderbilts.
Hosted the America's Cup sailing races from 1930 to 1983.
Bob Dylan famously went electric at its folk festival in 1965.

Q214164.name: Bellevue
facts: Lies across Lake Washington from Seattle, linked by floating bridges.
Video game company Valve, maker of Steam and Half-Life, is based here.
Phone carrier T-Mobile has its headquarters here.

Q159232.name: Santa Cruz
facts: Its seaside Boardwalk has the Giant Dipper, a wooden roller coaster from 1924.
Surfing was introduced to the mainland here by Hawaiian princes in 1885.
Sits on the north end of Monterey Bay; its university's mascot is the banana slug.

Q12829733.name: Belém
facts: A gateway to the Amazon, near the mouth of the great river.
Its Ver-o-Peso market is famous for açaí, fish and Amazonian produce.
Hosts the Círio de Nazaré, one of the world's largest religious processions.

Q1467.name: Cebu City
facts: Magellan's Cross, planted by the explorer in 1521, stands in the city centre.
Magellan was killed nearby on Mactan island by the chief Lapu-Lapu.
Famous for its Sinulog festival, roast lechon and dried mangoes.

Q132572.name: Tiraspol
facts: Capital of a breakaway strip of land that still flies the hammer and sickle.
Its Sheriff football club stunned Real Madrid in Madrid in 2021.
Sits on the Dniester River and is known for Kvint brandy.

Q515229.name: Ngerulmud
facts: Its domed capitol, opened in 2006, echoes the US Capitol in Washington.
Sits on Babeldaob island, replacing Koror as the seat of government.
One of the world's least-populous capitals, with hardly any residents.

Q82185.name: La Rochelle
facts: Its Old Port is guarded by medieval stone towers on the Bay of Biscay.
A Protestant stronghold besieged by Cardinal Richelieu in 1627-28.
Its World War II U-boat pens appear in the film Das Boot.

Q123766.name: Charlottesville
facts: Thomas Jefferson's home, Monticello, stands on a hilltop just outside the city.
Jefferson founded the university here, with its famous Lawn and Rotunda.
The Dave Matthews Band formed here, near the Blue Ridge Mountains.

Q44198.name: Brampton
facts: Nicknamed 'Flower Town' for the vast greenhouses that once grew roses here.
Actor Michael Cera and comedian Russell Peters grew up here.
A fast-growing suburb northwest of Toronto, near Pearson airport.

Q189471.name: Cupertino
facts: Home to Apple's ring-shaped headquarters, Apple Park.
Steve Jobs unveiled the original Macintosh here in 1984.
Lies in the heart of Silicon Valley, just west of San Jose.

Q327012.name: Bangor
facts: Horror novelist Stephen King lives here, and it inspired his town of Derry.
A giant statue of Paul Bunyan honours its days as a lumber capital.
Sits on the Penobscot River.

Q192700.name: Lake Placid
facts: Hosted the Winter Olympics twice, in 1932 and 1980.
The 'Miracle on Ice' hockey game was played here in 1980.
A village in the heart of the Adirondack Mountains.

Q192896.name: Carlisle
facts: Hadrian's Wall passes through, and its castle once held Mary, Queen of Scots.
Carr's crackers and biscuits have been made here since the 1830s.
Lies on the River Eden, about 10 miles from the border with Scotland.

Q203263.name: Athens
facts: Bands R.E.M. and the B-52's both formed here.
Home to 'the Tree That Owns Itself', said to have been deeded its own land.
Its big college football team plays 'Between the Hedges', about 70 miles from Atlanta.

Q232226.name: Kelowna
facts: Sits on Okanagan Lake, said to be home to the lake monster Ogopogo.
Surrounded by vineyards and orchards, it is a hub of wine country.
A floating bridge carries the highway across the lake here.

Q239870.name: Columbus
facts: Sits on the Chattahoochee River, which has an urban whitewater rafting course.
Fort Benning, home of the National Infantry Museum, is next door.
Coca-Cola inventor John Pemberton developed his early tonics here.

Q179046.name: Fatehpur Sikri
facts: Built by Mughal emperor Akbar as his capital, then abandoned soon after.
Its gateway, the Buland Darwaza, is one of the largest in the world.
A red sandstone city about 35 km west of Agra and the Taj Mahal.

Q41185.name: Caen
facts: William the Conqueror built its castle and is buried in its Abbaye aux Hommes.
Largely destroyed in the fierce 1944 battle after the D-Day landings.
Lies on the River Orne, just inland from the D-Day beaches.

Q44401.name: Cayenne
facts: A fiery red chili pepper shares its name.
The notorious Devil's Island penal colony, of Papillon fame, lies up the coast.
Europe's spaceport at Kourou is about an hour's drive away.

Q40811.name: Sokhumi
facts: A Black Sea resort beside a wide bay, backed by the Caucasus Mountains.
Founded as the ancient Greek colony of Dioscurias.
Home to a famous Soviet monkey-breeding research centre and an old botanical garden.

Q489197.name: Torrance
facts: Its high school played both Sunnydale High in Buffy and West Beverly in 90210.
Olympic runner and war hero Louis Zamperini grew up here.
Honda's main regional headquarters is here, beside Redondo Beach.

Q36260.name: Apia
facts: Robert Louis Stevenson lived at Vailima here and is buried on Mount Vaea.
In 1889 a cyclone wrecked American and German warships in its harbour.
Lies on the north coast of Upolu island in the South Pacific.

Q13369.name: Rimini
facts: Film director Federico Fellini was born here.
A popular Adriatic beach resort lined with umbrellas.
Its Roman Arch of Augustus and Bridge of Tiberius still stand.

Q128269.name: Frisco
facts: The Dallas Cowboys' headquarters and training centre, The Star, is here.
Home to the National Soccer Hall of Fame and the headquarters of the PGA, golf's pro association.
A booming suburb north of Dallas.

Q12193.name: Brest
facts: A major Atlantic naval base near the western tip of the mainland.
A ring-shaped praline pastry is named after a bike race from Paris to here and back.
Its old town was almost entirely destroyed in the 1944 siege.

Q171080.name: Kotor
facts: Sits at the end of a fjord-like bay on the Adriatic coast.
Its medieval walls climb steeply up the mountain to St John's fortress.
Famous for the many cats that roam its old town lanes.

Q278204.name: Noida
facts: A planned city across the Yamuna River from Delhi.
Its Film City is home to many TV studios and news channels.
The nearby Buddh circuit hosted Formula One races from 2011 to 2013.

Q384544.name: Karlovy Vary
facts: A spa town known in German as Karlsbad, named after Emperor Charles IV.
Birthplace of Becherovka, an herbal liqueur made with its spring water.
Hosts one of the oldest film festivals in the world.

Q79996.name: Nome
facts: The finish line of the Iditarod sled dog race.
In 1925, sled dogs including Balto raced diphtheria serum here.
A gold rush town on the Bering Sea; Wyatt Earp ran a saloon here.

Q173474.name: Veliko Tarnovo
facts: A medieval royal capital whose Tsarevets fortress sits on a hill.
The Yantra River winds through a deep gorge around the old town.
Its fortress hosts a dramatic sound-and-light show at night.

Q131127.name: Banja Luka
facts: Sits on the Vrbas River, popular for whitewater rafting.
Its Ferhadija Mosque, destroyed in 1993, was rebuilt and reopened in 2016.
Much of the city was rebuilt after a severe earthquake in 1969.

Q125293.name: Heroica Puebla de Zaragoza
facts: Cinco de Mayo commemorates a victory over French troops here in 1862.
Mole sauce and chiles en nogada are said to have been created here.
Famous for Talavera pottery and views of the Popocatépetl volcano.

Q1880.name: Concepción
facts: Badly hit by the magnitude 8.8 earthquake and tsunami of 2010.
Moved inland from Penco in the 1700s after earthquakes and tsunamis.
Lies near the Pacific beside the port of Talcahuano.

Q205842.name: Aspen
facts: A glamorous ski town in the Rocky Mountains, near the Maroon Bells.
Began as a silver-mining boomtown in the 1880s.
Gonzo writer Hunter S. Thompson ran for county sheriff here in 1970.

Q28206.name: Augusta
facts: Sits on the Kennebec River.
Old Fort Western, built in 1754, is said to be the oldest wooden fort in the nation.
Its granite capitol was designed by Charles Bulfinch.

Q3909.name: Maseru
facts: Capital of a mountain kingdom entirely surrounded by South Africa.
Sits on the Caledon River, right on the border.
A craft shop here is shaped like the traditional conical straw hat.

Q2795.name: Chemnitz
facts: Called Karl-Marx-Stadt from 1953 to 1990.
A giant 7-metre bronze head of Karl Marx stands in the city centre.
A textile boomtown once nicknamed a 'Manchester', and 2025 European Capital of Culture.

Q165204.name: Mérida
facts: Known as 'the White City', it was built on the stones of the Maya city of T'hó.
Chichén Itzá and Uxmal are within day-trip reach.
Famous for cochinita pibil, slow-roasted pork marinated in achiote.

Q103717.name: Rovaniemi
facts: Calls itself the official hometown of Santa Claus, with a village on the Arctic Circle.
Alvar Aalto planned its rebuilt streets in the shape of reindeer antlers.
Burned almost entirely in 1944, it is a top spot for seeing the northern lights.

Q184163.name: Colchester
facts: Claims to be its country's oldest recorded town, the Roman Camulodunum.
Queen Boudica burned it to the ground in AD 60.
Its castle has the largest Norman keep in Europe.

Q28603.name: Frankfort
facts: Frontiersman Daniel Boone is buried in its cemetery.
The Buffalo Trace bourbon distillery is here.
Its capitol is known for a huge floral clock on the lawn.

Q3043.name: Belmopan
facts: Built inland after Hurricane Hattie devastated the old coastal capital in 1961.
Its National Assembly building is modelled on a Maya temple.
The smallest capital by population in the continental Americas.

Q228405.name: Madurai
facts: The Meenakshi Amman Temple, with its towering painted gopurams, dominates the city.
Sits on the Vaigai River and is called the 'City of Jasmine'.
Famous for jigarthanda, a cold drink of milk, almond gum and ice cream.

Q128295.name: Abilene
facts: Dyess Air Force Base here is home to B-1 bombers.
Called the 'Storybook Capital', with sculptures of children's book characters downtown.
Singer Jessica Simpson was born here.

Q2126436.name: Ras al-Khaimah
facts: Jebel Jais, the highest peak in the federation, rises behind the city.
Its mountain has one of the world's longest ziplines.
Lies in the north, between the Hajar Mountains and the Gulf, near the ancient port of Julfar.

Q234053.name: Vancouver
facts: Lies on the Columbia River directly across from Portland, Oregon.
Grew from a Hudson's Bay Company fur-trading fort founded in 1825.
Mount St. Helens rises about 50 miles to the northeast.

Q199909.name: Karbala
facts: Site of the battle in 680 AD where the Prophet's grandson Husayn was killed.
The golden-domed Shrine of Imam Husayn is one of Shia Islam's holiest sites.
Millions walk here each year for Arbaeen, one of the world's largest gatherings.

Q51599.name: Punta Arenas
facts: Lies on the Strait of Magellan, one of the world's southernmost cities.
A gateway for ships and flights to Antarctica.
Touching the foot of a statue in its plaza is said to ensure you'll return.

Q34116.name: Thunder Bay
facts: Sits on Lake Superior, facing the Sleeping Giant rock formation.
Terry Fox's Marathon of Hope ended near here, marked by a monument.
Its huge grain elevators once shipped prairie wheat across the Great Lakes.

Q761.name: Białystok
facts: Ludwik Zamenhof, creator of Esperanto, was born here.
Its Branicki Palace is nicknamed the 'Versailles of the North'.
Near the Białowieża Forest, home of wild European bison.

Q172438.name: Peterborough
facts: Catherine of Aragon is buried in its cathedral.
Sits on the River Nene; its football club is nicknamed 'the Posh'.
Famous for brickmaking, with clay pits that supplied London Brick.

Q93338.name: Gaziantep
facts: Famed for baklava and pistachios.
Its Zeugma Mosaic Museum holds the famous 'Gypsy Girl' mosaic.
Lies near the Syrian border; called Aintab in the past.

Q49244.name: Santa Ana
facts: Hot, dry desert winds that sweep the region share its name.
Home to the Bowers Museum, a few miles south of Disneyland.
The county seat of Orange County, with its historic red-stone courthouse.

Q490584.name: Flint
facts: General Motors was founded here in 1908.
Known for a water crisis that began in 2014 when lead leached into its supply.
Michael Moore's film Roger & Me documented its auto plant closures.

Q3854.name: Bujumbura
facts: Lies at the northeastern tip of Lake Tanganyika.
Was the national capital until Gitega took over the role in 2019.
The border with the Democratic Republic of the Congo is just to the west.

Q200054.name: Jamshedpur
facts: Named after Jamsetji Tata, it grew around Tata Steel's first plant.
Also called Tatanagar, it is a planned company town.
Sits at the confluence of the Subarnarekha and Kharkai rivers.

Q82174.name: Brașov
facts: Its Gothic Black Church got its name from a fire in 1689.
A Hollywood-style sign sits on Tâmpa mountain above the old town.
Bran Castle, sold to tourists as 'Dracula's Castle', is nearby in the Carpathians.

Q200019.name: Jodhpur
facts: Known as the 'Blue City' for its indigo-painted houses.
The mighty Mehrangarh Fort towers over it on a cliff.
A style of riding trousers is named after it; it sits on the edge of the Thar Desert.

Q33518.name: Dover
facts: Its Air Force base receives the remains of military members killed overseas.
Its NASCAR oval is nicknamed 'the Monster Mile'.
Caesar Rodney rode from here to Philadelphia in 1776 to vote for independence.

Q180057.name: Lincoln
facts: Its cathedral was the tallest building in the world for over 200 years.
One of the original Magna Carta copies is kept in its castle.
The first tanks were built here in World War I, by the firm William Foster & Co.

Q501796.name: Roanoke
facts: A giant illuminated star on Mill Mountain gives it the nickname 'Star City'.
A historic railroad town, once headquarters of the Norfolk and Western Railway.
Lies in a valley of the Blue Ridge Mountains, near the Blue Ridge Parkway.

Q23443.name: Provo
facts: Home to Brigham Young University.
Mount Timpanogos and the Wasatch Range rise right behind the city.
Robert Redford's Sundance resort is up the canyon nearby.

Q40747.name: Pierre
facts: Locals pronounce its name 'peer'.
Sits on the Missouri River, near the huge Oahe Dam.
One of the few state capitals not served by an interstate highway.

Q3014.name: Wolfsburg
facts: Volkswagen's headquarters and giant factory are here; the city was founded for it in 1938.
The Autostadt delivers new cars from glass towers.
Lies on the Aller river and the Mittelland Canal; Zaha Hadid designed its phaeno science centre.

Q200340.name: Udaipur
facts: Called the 'City of Lakes', with the Lake Palace on Lake Pichola.
The James Bond film Octopussy was filmed here.
Its vast City Palace overlooks the lake, in the Aravalli hills.

Q167155.name: Kalamazoo
facts: Gibson guitars were first made here.
A Glenn Miller hit song is named after the city.
Checker taxicabs were built here; it was also home to the Upjohn drug company.

Q28729.name: Kozhikode
facts: Vasco da Gama landed near here in 1498, opening the sea route from Europe.
Calico cotton cloth takes its name from the city's old name, Calicut.
A Malabar Coast spice port, famous for its sweet halwa.

Q6730.name: Perpignan
facts: Sits on the Roussillon plain at the foot of the Pyrenees, a short drive from the Mediterranean and the Spanish border.
Its Palace of the Kings of Majorca recalls its time as a mainland capital of that medieval kingdom.
Salvador Dalí called its railway station the centre of the universe.

Q36262.name: St. John's
facts: Its cathedral's twin white towers rise above a harbour busy with cruise ships.
Brian Lara made Test cricket's highest innings, 400 not out, at its Recreation Ground in 2004.
The island it sits on is famous for claiming a beach for every day of the year.

Q128361.name: Odessa
facts: An oil town in the Permian Basin of the west, next door to its rival Midland.
Its Permian High School football team inspired the book and TV series Friday Night Lights.
A meteor crater lies just outside town, and a university campus holds a full-size Stonehenge replica.

Q47048.name: Oulu
facts: A northern port at the mouth of its namesake river on the Gulf of Bothnia.
It hosts the Air Guitar World Championships every summer.
A big tech hub that grew around Nokia, it was a European Capital of Culture in 2026.

Q462177.name: White Plains
facts: George Washington fought the British at a 1776 battle here, north of Manhattan.
The state's congress approved the Declaration of Independence here in July 1776.
A Westchester County suburb about 25 miles north of Midtown Manhattan.

Q629088.name: Calabasas
facts: A gated celebrity enclave where several Kardashians and Jenners have homes.
Its name comes from the Spanish word for squashes or pumpkins.
Nestled in the Santa Monica Mountains on the edge of the San Fernando Valley.

Q172668.name: Fugging
facts: Its old name was so rude in English that tourists kept stealing the signs, so it changed its spelling in 2021.
A tiny village a short drive north of Salzburg.
Lies just east of the Inn river, which marks the German border here.

Q79857.name: Konya
facts: The Sufi poet Rumi is buried here, and whirling dervishes still perform in his honour.
Known in ancient times and in the Bible as Iconium, visited by the Apostle Paul.
Sits on the vast Anatolian Plateau, near the Neolithic site of Çatalhöyük.

Q132997.name: Florianópolis
facts: Mostly on an island, linked to the mainland by the Hercílio Luz suspension bridge.
Nicknamed the 'Island of Magic', it is loved for surf beaches like Joaquina.
Tennis star Gustavo 'Guga' Kuerten, three-time French Open champion, was born here.

Q43631.name: Leiden
facts: Rembrandt was born here, on the Old Rhine.
Home of the country's oldest university, founded in 1575, where superconductivity was discovered in 1911.
The Pilgrims lived here for about a decade before sailing on the Mayflower.

Q462799.name: Evanston
facts: Home of Northwestern University, on the Lake Michigan shore just north of Chicago.
The Woman's Christian Temperance Union is based here, and the town stayed 'dry' for decades.
One of several places claiming to have invented the ice cream sundae.

Q170525.name: Agadir
facts: An Atlantic beach resort near where the Souss River meets the ocean, below the Atlas Mountains.
Rebuilt from scratch after a devastating earthquake in 1960.
The hilltop kasbah ruin is inscribed with 'God, Country, King'; argan trees grow in the hinterland.

Q7951.name: Petropavlovsk-Kamchatsky
facts: Overlooked by the snow-capped Koryaksky and Avachinsky volcanoes on Avacha Bay.
Named after Vitus Bering's two ships, the St. Peter and St. Paul.
No road connects it to the rest of the country; you arrive by sea or air.

Q690.name: Delft
facts: Gave its name to famous blue-and-white tin-glazed pottery.
Painter Johannes Vermeer was born and worked here, and painted a famous view of the town.
William the Silent was assassinated here in 1584; the royal family is buried in its New Church.

Q13496.name: Brindisi
facts: Roman columns here mark the end of the Appian Way from Rome.
The poet Virgil died here in 19 BC on his way back from Greece.
An Adriatic port near the heel of the boot, with ferries across to Greece.

Q4656.name: Pula
facts: Home to one of the best-preserved Roman amphitheatres in the world.
James Joyce taught English here in 1904-05.
Near the Brijuni Islands, where Yugoslav leader Tito kept a summer residence.

Q776965.name: Klaipėda
facts: Long known by its German name Memel, it is the country's only seaport.
Ferries cross from here to the Curonian Spit and its towering sand dunes.
A statue of Ännchen von Tharau, heroine of a famous folk song, stands in its theatre square.

Q130800.name: Papeete
facts: The main town of Tahiti, in the South Pacific.
Paul Gauguin sailed here in 1891 and painted the island's people.
A market town famous for black pearls and the Heiva dance festival.

Q170497.name: Gloucester
facts: Its cathedral cloisters stood in for Hogwarts corridors in the Harry Potter films.
Sits on the River Severn between the Cotswolds and the Forest of Dean.
King Edward II is buried in the cathedral; Beatrix Potter set a tailor's tale here.

Q47554.name: Toruń
facts: Nicolaus Copernicus was born here in 1473.
Famous for its gingerbread, baked here since the Middle Ages.
A medieval Teutonic Knights town on the Vistula River.

Q1476.name: Le Mans
facts: Hosts a world-famous 24-hour endurance car race, first run in 1923.
England's King Henry II, first of the Plantagenets, was born here.
Its old town sits inside some of the best-preserved Roman walls, on the Sarthe River.

Q5332.name: Saratov
facts: A big port on the Volga River, crossed here by long bridges.
Yuri Gagarin parachuted down in fields nearby after the first human spaceflight in 1961.
Gagarin had learned to fly at a flying club here as a student.

Q131350.name: Nishapur
facts: Poet and astronomer Omar Khayyam was born and buried here.
The mystic poet Attar, author of The Conference of the Birds, also lies here.
Long famed for nearby turquoise mines, on the Silk Road route to Central Asia.

Q160642.name: Salisbury
facts: Its cathedral has the tallest church spire in the land and the best-preserved Magna Carta.
Stonehenge stands on the plain about eight miles to the north.
Former Russian spy Sergei Skripal was poisoned with Novichok here in 2018.

Q200663.name: Faridabad
facts: An industrial satellite city just south of Delhi, with the Yamuna River on its east.
Hosts the Surajkund crafts fair every February.
Founded in 1607 by Shaikh Farid, treasurer of Mughal emperor Jahangir.

Q169134.name: Nara
facts: Hundreds of tame deer roam its park and bow to visitors for crackers.
Todai-ji temple houses a giant bronze Buddha in a vast wooden hall.
Became the country's first permanent capital in 710.

Q244146.name: Clearwater
facts: Its white-sand beach on the Gulf of Mexico regularly tops best-beach lists.
Spiritual headquarters of the Church of Scientology, and birthplace of Hooters.
Winter, the dolphin with a prosthetic tail from the film Dolphin Tale, lived at its aquarium.

Q118958.name: Leuven
facts: Stella Artois is brewed here, and the world's biggest brewer AB InBev is based here.
Its university, founded in 1425, is one of the oldest in Europe.
Its university library was burned by German troops in 1914 and rebuilt with American help.

Q102728.name: Ypres
facts: The scene of brutal World War I battles, nicknamed 'Wipers' by British soldiers.
Buglers play the Last Post every evening under the Menin Gate memorial.
At its Cat Parade festival, toy cats are thrown from the Cloth Hall belfry.

Q2337.name: Smolensk
facts: An ancient fortress city on the upper Dnieper River, on the road between Moscow and Europe.
The Katyn massacre site lies just outside the city.
The Polish president's plane crashed on approach to its airport in 2010.

Q1848.name: San Marino
facts: Three medieval towers crown Monte Titano above the old town.
Its republic claims to be the world's oldest, founded in 301 by a stonemason named Marinus.
A hilltop capital of a microstate surrounded entirely by Italy.

Q486860.name: Mountain View
facts: Google's headquarters, the Googleplex, is here.
Shockley Semiconductor opened here in 1956, helping launch Silicon Valley.
Home of the Computer History Museum and NASA's Ames Research Center at Moffett Field.

Q79873.name: Tombstone
facts: The Gunfight at the O.K. Corral took place here in 1881.
Wyatt Earp and Doc Holliday made it famous; outlaws rest in Boothill Graveyard.
A silver boomtown in the desert nicknamed 'The Town Too Tough to Die'.

Q2486.name: Tarawa
facts: An atoll in the central Pacific, close to the Equator.
The site of one of the bloodiest battles of World War II in the Pacific, in November 1943.
Its long, thin southern islets are linked by causeways around a lagoon.

Q6231.name: Cremona
facts: Antonio Stradivari made his legendary violins here, as did the Amati and Guarneri families.
Its Torrazzo is one of the tallest brick bell towers in the world.
Sits on the Po river, and is famed for torrone nougat and composer Claudio Monteverdi.

Q43463.name: Fortaleza
facts: Its name means 'fortress', after a Dutch fort built here in the 1600s.
Fishermen still sail traditional log rafts called jangadas off its Atlantic beaches.
Home to Beach Park, one of Latin America's largest water parks, close to the Equator.

Q457334.name: Moncton
facts: Its Magnetic Hill makes cars appear to roll uphill.
The tidal bore from the Bay of Fundy rushes up the Petitcodiac River here.
Nicknamed the 'Hub City' for sitting at the heart of the Maritime Provinces.

Q189901.name: Argos
facts: One of the oldest continuously inhabited cities in the world.
In Homer, the Greeks are often called 'Argives' after it; Diomedes was its king.
In the Peloponnese near Mycenae and Nafplio, with a huge ancient theatre.

Q47034.name: Espoo
facts: Nokia and Angry Birds maker Rovio are headquartered here.
Home of Aalto University and the forest lakes of Nuuksio National Park.
Lies just west of Helsinki on the Gulf of Finland.

Q58900.name: Doncaster
facts: Named after the River Don; the St Leger, the oldest classic horse race, is run here.
The record-breaking steam locomotives Mallard and Flying Scotsman were built at its works.
Sits on the East Coast Main Line between London and Edinburgh.

Q486877.name: South Bend
facts: Named for the bend of the St. Joseph River; the University of Notre Dame is on its edge.
Studebaker built wagons and cars here for over a century.
Pete Buttigieg was its mayor before running for president.

Q3901.name: Moroni
facts: Sits on Grande Comore, below the active Mount Karthala volcano.
Its name means 'at the river' in the local language.
The islands around it are famed for vanilla and ylang-ylang perfume oil.

Q6537.name: Vicenza
facts: Architect Andrea Palladio filled it with buildings, giving us the word 'Palladian'.
Home of Palladio's Teatro Olimpico, the oldest surviving indoor theatre with a stage set.
Sits at the foot of Monte Berico, between Verona and Padua.

Q486439.name: Cedar Rapids
facts: Huge Quaker Oats and other cereal mills give the air a toasty smell.
Painter Grant Wood of American Gothic fame lived and worked here.
The Cedar River flooded much of downtown in 2008.

Q204561.name: Modesto
facts: George Lucas grew up here, and it inspired his film American Graffiti.
An arch downtown reads 'Water Wealth Contentment Health'.
In the Central Valley, home to the vast E. & J. Gallo winery.

Q68481.name: Fuzhou
facts: Known as Banyan City for the banyan trees planted across it.
Sits on the Min River estuary, facing Taiwan across the strait.
Famous for jasmine tea and its preserved 'Three Lanes and Seven Alleys' old quarter.

Q16868.name: Laredo
facts: Sits on the north bank of the Rio Grande, facing its twin city across the river.
One of the busiest inland trade ports in the Americas, with huge truck traffic.
A famous cowboy ballad is named after its streets.

Q92161.name: Changchun
facts: As Hsinking, it was the capital of the Japanese puppet state of Manchukuo.
Last emperor Puyi's Puppet Palace is preserved here.
Called the 'Motor City' of the country, home of carmaker FAW.

Q749.name: Groningen
facts: Its Martini Tower has watched over the main square since the 1400s.
A lively student city whose university was founded in 1614.
Europe's largest natural gas field lies nearby, causing small earthquakes.

Q28249.name: Concord
facts: Its gold-domed granite State House is one of the oldest still in use.
The sturdy stagecoaches that carried mail and passengers across the Wild West were built here.
Teacher-astronaut Christa McAuliffe taught at its high school before the Challenger disaster.

Q10389.name: Bandung
facts: Hosted the landmark 1955 Asian-African Conference of newly independent nations.
A cool highland city nicknamed 'Paris of Java', ringed by volcanoes like Tangkuban Perahu.
Home of the prestigious Institute of Technology, alma mater of President Sukarno.

Q163749.name: West Palm Beach
facts: Founded by railroad tycoon Henry Flagler for workers at his resort hotels.
Sits across Lake Worth Lagoon from the barrier island home of Mar-a-Lago.
Home of the Norton Museum of Art on the Atlantic coast north of Miami.

Q138578.name: Hoboken
facts: Frank Sinatra was born here.
The first recorded organized baseball game was played here in 1846.
Faces Manhattan across the Hudson River; On the Waterfront was filmed on its docks.

Q288.name: Tours
facts: Sits on the Loire, a gateway to the famous valley of chateaux.
Charles Martel halted an invading Umayyad army near here in 732.
Novelist Honoré de Balzac was born here; its patron is Saint Martin.

Q211907.name: Slough
facts: The original version of the sitcom The Office was set at a paper merchant here.
John Betjeman's poem begged 'Come, friendly bombs' to fall on it.
Mars bars have been made here since 1932; Windsor Castle is just across the Thames.

Q234061.name: Erie
facts: Its Presque Isle peninsula curves into the lake to form a sheltered bay.
Oliver Hazard Perry's War of 1812 fleet was built here.
Perry's restored flagship, the brig Niagara, is based at its waterfront.

Q49261.name: Mesa
facts: The Chicago Cubs hold spring training here, at Sloan Park.
A big desert suburb east of Phoenix along the Salt River.
Its name is Spanish for 'table', after the flat land it sits on.

Q192098.name: Oymyakon
facts: Called the coldest permanently inhabited place on Earth.
A temperature of about -67.7 C was recorded here in 1933.
Reached via the Kolyma Highway, the 'Road of Bones' built by Gulag prisoners.

Q33264.name: Las Cruces
facts: The jagged Organ Mountains rise to its east above the Rio Grande valley.
Billy the Kid was tried in neighbouring Mesilla's courthouse.
Close to White Sands and Spaceport America; its name means 'the crosses'.

Q3604.name: Djibouti
facts: Sits on the Gulf of Tadjoura near the Bab-el-Mandeb strait into the Red Sea.
Hosts the only permanent US military base in Africa, Camp Lemonnier.
Lake Assal, Africa's lowest point, lies inland from here.

Q173985.name: Faisalabad
facts: Called Lyallpur until 1979, when it was renamed after King Faisal of Saudi Arabia.
Its clock tower stands at the centre of eight bazaars laid out like the Union Jack.
A textile powerhouse, and hometown of qawwali singer Nusrat Fateh Ali Khan.

Q133123.name: Patras
facts: Hosts one of Europe's biggest carnivals.
The Rio-Antirrio cable bridge spans the gulf next to it.
Saint Andrew is said to have been martyred here; his basilica is one of the region's largest.

Q230818.name: Leh
facts: Its old palace towers over town like a smaller version of Lhasa's Potala.
Sits at about 3,500 m in the Himalayas, near the Indus River.
Gateway to Khardung La, one of the world's highest motorable passes, and Pangong Lake.

Q721455.name: Miami Gardens
facts: Home of Hard Rock Stadium, where the Dolphins play and Super Bowls are held.
A Formula 1 Grand Prix is raced on a track around its stadium.
A suburb just north of Miami; the Miami Open tennis tournament is played here.

Q200942.name: Swindon
facts: Grew around Brunel's Great Western Railway works.
Famous for its 'Magic Roundabout', five mini-roundabouts around a central one.
Sits on the M4 between London and Bristol, at the edge of the Cotswolds.

Q3852.name: Worms
facts: Martin Luther refused to recant before the Emperor at an imperial Diet here in 1521.
A setting of the Nibelungenlied epic, on the Rhine.
Its medieval Jewish community, with scholar Rashi, is a UNESCO site; Liebfraumilch wine began here.

Q102158.name: Narva
facts: Its castle faces Ivangorod fortress across the river border with Russia.
Most residents speak Russian as their first language.
Sits at the country's eastern tip, on the river border a few miles from the Gulf of Finland.

Q219656.name: Macon
facts: Hometown of Little Richard and Otis Redding; the Allman Brothers Band started here.
Its Cherry Blossom Festival celebrates hundreds of thousands of Yoshino cherry trees.
Native American earthworks of Ocmulgee Mounds rise on the river's edge.

Q25409.name: Košice
facts: Europe's oldest marathon has been run here every year since 1924.
Its St. Elisabeth Cathedral is the easternmost Gothic cathedral in Western Christianity.
On the river Hornád near the Hungarian and Ukrainian borders.

Q79808.name: Constanța
facts: Founded as ancient Tomis, where the Roman poet Ovid lived out his exile.
The country's main port, on the Black Sea.
Its Art Nouveau casino stands on the seafront promenade.

Q43453.name: Plzeň
facts: Pilsner lager was invented here in 1842 and is named after the city.
Home of the Škoda engineering works.
Liberated by General Patton's US army in 1945, between Prague and the German border.

Q502141.name: Rishikesh
facts: The Beatles studied meditation at an ashram here in 1968.
Known as the yoga capital of the world, on the Ganges at the foot of the Himalayas.
