Pilgrims cross the river on the Lakshman Jhula and Ram Jhula footbridges.

Q29888.name: Aswan
facts: The High Dam just upstream holds back the Nile to form Lake Nasser.
The island temple of Philae and the Unfinished Obelisk are nearby.
Felucca sailboats glide past Elephantine Island; it's the jumping-off point for Abu Simbel.

Q13386.name: Lecce
facts: Called the 'Florence of the South' for its ornate Baroque churches.
Built of soft, honey-coloured local limestone that is easy to carve.
In the heel of the boot, on the Salento peninsula between two seas.

Q491540.name: Sarasota
facts: Winter home of the Ringling Brothers circus; John Ringling's museum is here.
Nearby Siesta Key is famous for its powder-soft white quartz sand.
Sits on a Gulf Coast bay south of Tampa.

Q127063.name: Kars
facts: The setting of Orhan Pamuk's novel Snow.
The ruined medieval Armenian capital of Ani lies nearby on the border.
Ruled by Russia from 1878 to 1918, leaving Russian-style buildings; famed for its cheese and honey.

Q4100.name: Baden-Baden
facts: A spa town since the Romans, with grand bathhouses at the edge of the Black Forest.
Dostoevsky gambled away money at its famous casino.
Lies just east of the Rhine, a few miles from the French border.

Q244898.name: New Taipei City
facts: Completely surrounds Taipei.
Includes the hillside teahouse town of Jiufen and the sunset harbour of Tamsui.
Yehliu's 'Queen's Head' rock and Pingxi's sky lanterns are here.

Q101254.name: Newport
facts: Its Transporter Bridge carries cars across the River Usk in a hanging gondola.
The Chartist rising of 1839 ended in a deadly clash here.
The Celtic Manor resort here hosted golf's 2010 Ryder Cup.

Q25331.name: Odense
facts: Hans Christian Andersen was born here.
Its name comes from the god Odin's sanctuary.
The main city of the island of Funen, birthplace of composer Carl Nielsen nearby.

Q168193.name: Najaf
facts: The golden-domed Imam Ali Shrine is here, a holy site of Shia Islam.
Its Wadi al-Salam cemetery is one of the largest in the world.
A centre of Shia learning, south of Baghdad near ancient Kufa.

Q42168.name: Clermont-Ferrand
facts: Michelin tyres were born here and the company is still based here.
Overlooked by the Puy de Dôme volcano; its cathedral is built of black lava stone.
Pope Urban II launched the First Crusade here in 1095; Blaise Pascal was born here.

Q15684.name: Segovia
facts: A towering two-tier Roman aqueduct runs through its old town.
Its fairytale Alcázar castle sits on a rocky prow above two rivers.
Famous for cochinillo, roast suckling pig carved with a plate.

Q184090.name: Preston
facts: Its football club were the first league champions, the unbeaten 'Invincibles' of 1888-89.
Holds a festival called the Guild just once every 20 years.
Sits on the River Ribble; its bypass was the first stretch of motorway in the country.

Q80041.name: Sedona
facts: Surrounded by red sandstone formations like Cathedral Rock and Bell Rock.
New Age visitors flock to its energy 'vortexes'.
Its Chapel of the Holy Cross is built into the red cliffs, south of Flagstaff.

Q34126.name: Funafuti
facts: A ring of low coral islets in the South Pacific, threatened by rising seas.
Its airport runway doubles as a football pitch and playground.
Scientists drilled its coral in the 1890s to test Darwin's theory of atolls.

Q9920.name: Haarlem
facts: Harlem in New York City was named after it.
Painter Frans Hals worked here; his museum is in town.
Home of Corrie ten Boom's house and Teylers, the country's oldest museum.

Q216820.name: Youngstown
facts: A former steel town on the Mahoning River between Cleveland and Pittsburgh.
Bruce Springsteen sang about its shuttered steel mills.
The Warner brothers of Hollywood grew up here.

Q203476.name: Srivijayapuram
facts: Formerly Port Blair, it was renamed in 2024.
Its Cellular Jail held independence fighters in solitary cells.
Gateway to tropical islands in the Bay of Bengal, with the ruins of Ross Island offshore.

Q38834.name: Nukuʻalofa
facts: Its white wooden Royal Palace dates from 1867 and faces the sea.
Among the first capitals to greet each new day, just west of the date line.
The island it sits on has the Ha'amonga 'a Maui stone trilithon.

Q41295.name: Basseterre
facts: Its central 'Circus' and clock tower were modelled on London's Piccadilly Circus.
Founded by the French, its name means 'low land'.
Brimstone Hill Fortress, a UNESCO site, stands on the same island.

Q40921.name: Honiara
facts: On Guadalcanal, scene of a major World War II campaign.
Its airport was originally Henderson Field, the WWII airstrip.
The waters offshore are called Iron Bottom Sound for all the sunken warships.

Q37806.name: Port Vila
facts: Sits on a harbour of Efate island in the South Pacific.
Was the capital of the New Hebrides, jointly run by Britain and France.
Devastated by Cyclone Pam in 2015; the Mele Cascades waterfalls are nearby.

Q41547.name: St. George's
facts: Its horseshoe harbour, the Carenage, fills an old volcanic crater.
Capital of the 'Spice Isle', famed for nutmeg.
US troops landed here in the 1983 invasion.

Q42751.name: Palikir
facts: Became the capital in 1989, replacing the nearby port town of Kolonia.
The ancient basalt city of Nan Madol lies on the same island.
Lies on one of the rainiest islands on Earth in the western Pacific.

Q41699.name: Castries
facts: Nobel poet Derek Walcott was born here.
The twin volcanic Pitons stand to the south on the same island.
Repeatedly destroyed by fire; it sits on a sheltered harbour used by cruise ships.

Q36281.name: Roseau
facts: Gateway to the Boiling Lake and Morne Trois Pitons National Park.
Novelist Jean Rhys, author of Wide Sargasso Sea, was born here.
Hit hard by Hurricane Maria in 2017, on the island's Caribbean coast.

Q3274.name: Managua
facts: Sits on the shore of Lake Xolotlán, with Momotombo volcano across the water.
A 1972 earthquake destroyed its downtown and old cathedral.
Giant metal 'Trees of Life' light up its avenues.

Q41474.name: Kingstown
facts: Its botanical garden, founded in 1765, is the oldest in the Western Hemisphere.
Captain Bligh brought breadfruit to the island's gardens in 1793.
Pirates of the Caribbean was filmed at Wallilabou Bay on the same island.

Q31026.name: Yaren District
facts: The country has no official capital; this district hosts parliament and government offices.
The island's airport runway takes up much of the district.
On a tiny Pacific island stripped by phosphate mining; Moqua Well is an underground lake here.
